title: Billing Specialist
description: It has to make sense. That is the standard at Divorce With A Plan. Not "close enough." Not "that is just how billing works." It has to make sense to the client, or we have not done our job. Clients are high-net-worth professionals going through divorce across the state of Maryland. They are intelligent, capable people navigating a financial experience they were never trained for. They do not know what an evergreen retainer is. They do not know what a trust replenishment request means or why it matters. And if no one explains it in a way that makes sense to them, they lose confidence in the process, and they lose sight of the plan they are working toward. That is the problem this role solves. The Billing Specialist at Divorce With A Plan is the person who makes the financial side of a divorce case make sense to the client. You walk beside them from the day they retain the firm through the day the case closes, connecting every payment to the outcome they are working toward. You are part of their walk. You are the one who helps them see that the $5,000 retainer replenishment is not just a number. It is the next step toward the custody arrangement they need, the property division that protects their future, the agreement that lets them move forward. The time you spend with clients explaining their billing, answering their questions, and making sure their plan still makes sense to them is not an extra. It is not a favor. It is part of the service. There is no additional cost to the client for the time you invest in making sure they understand. That is how this firm works, and it is one of the reasons clients trust us. How we do it: the right way. This firm runs on structure. There is a defined process for everything, because when the process is clear, the client gets a consistent experience no matter which attorney is on their case or which week of the month it is. You will have a daily call block schedule so clients are never waiting days for a return call. You will have a billing script built on the Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct so clients hear accurate, compliant information every time. You will have an escalation protocol with documented timestamps, so no client concern sits unaddressed. You will have a weekly deliverable that captures how clients are feeling, what they need, and what feedback they are giving us, so the firm can respond to what clients are actually experiencing, not what we assume they are experiencing. If you are someone who finds relief in knowing exactly what the standard is, exactly what a good day looks like, and exactly what is expected, keep reading. What you produce: a contribution that protects the client and the firm. The Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct require that clients be kept informed about the status of their matter (Rule 1.4), that fees are reasonable and clearly communicated (Rule 1.5), and that client funds held in trust are safeguarded with precision (Rule 1.15). Those rules exist to protect the client. Everything this role does is built around upholding them. Every call you make either keeps a client informed or it does not. Every replenishment conversation either connects the payment to the client's goals and gives them the information they are entitled to, or it leaves them making financial decisions without the full picture. Every trust balance you monitor either gets flagged the same day it drops below threshold, protecting the client's funds and the firm's fiduciary obligation, or it becomes the kind of gap that puts both at risk. You are not here to process invoices. You are here to contribute to something that matters: a client's ability to get through the hardest financial experience of their life with clarity, dignity, and a plan that makes sense to them, while ensuring the fir ---------- ets the professional standards that make all of that possible. Here is who thrives in this role. You genuinely like people. Not in theory. In practice. You are energized by 20+ phone conversations a day because you actually want to know how someone is doing, and they can tell the difference. You remember that a client's daughter just started high school, that another client lost their job two months ago, that someone told you in March they were scared about the mediation in May, and when you call in May, you ask about it before you ask about the balance. You are organized because you cannot function without a system. You manage 100 to 150 active client relationships, and nothing falls through because you built something (a spreadsheet, a calendar, a color-coded tracker, a handwritten list) that keeps you moving. You do not wait for someone to tell you what needs attention. You see the attorney's calendar, you see the hearing in two weeks, and you pick up the phone, because the client deserves to know what is coming before it arrives. You have the emotional range to sit with a client who is crying about their financial situation on Tuesday and have a firm, direct conversation about a past-due balance on Wednesday, and both conversations are authentic because both come from the same place: you care about this person's outcome, and you are going to tell them the truth. You have been described as "the person who can get anyone to pay," and you know the reason is not pressure. It is trust. People pay you because you took the time to help them understand what they were paying for and why it mattered to their case. Here is who this role is not for. 1. If you want to process invoices in a back office and never talk to a client, this role will make you miserable. 2. If you avoid difficult conversations about money, you will not survive the first month. These clients are going through a divorce. Money is emotional. You need to be able to hold that space and still move the conversation forward, because the client needs someone who will stay in it with them. 3. If you need someone to tell you what to do every hour, this is not the right structure for you. You will have clear expectations, daily blocks, and weekly deliverables. Within that framework, you think, prioritize, and act. Problems get fixed or flagged, because a problem that sits is a client who waits. If you read from a script without understanding why each line exists, you will fail here. Every call requires context. You know what is happening in the client's case before you dial, and you lead with that, because a client who feels known is a client who stays engaged in their own plan. If the phrase "it has to make sense" does not resonate with you at a gut level, if you are comfortable with "good enough" or "that is just how we do it," you will not be happy working here. Responsibilities 1. Make the Financial Side of the Case Make Sense from Day One 2. Within five business days of retention, deliver a billing tutorial covering retainer structure, evergreen replenishment, invoice format, and what to expect at each stage, so the client starts their case understanding how the financial side works before they receive their first invoice. 3. Conduct a live introductory call to walk through the material, answer questions, and establish the relationship. This call gives the client a person they can reach when billing feels confusing, and it gives you the context to serve them well for the life of their case. 4. Provide specific dollar ranges for upcoming cost events (hearings: $5,000-$10,000, mediations, trials: $15,000-$30,000) so the client can plan ahead instead of reacting to surprises. 5. Introduce yourself as a non-billable point of contact. The time you spend making sure their plan still makes sense to them is part of the service, not an add-on. Clients who know they can call you without a meter running are clients who stay informed and engaged. 6. Keep Trust Accounts Funded by Keeping Clients Informed 7. Monitor trust balances daily across ---------- active matters so no client's case is disrupted by a funding gap they did not see coming. 8. Call every client before sending a replenishment request. No email goes out without a phone call attempt. The call comes first because the client deserves a conversation, not a demand. 9. When requesting additional retainers for upcoming events, reference the specific event by name and the date you first discussed it. This tells the client you are paying attention to their case, not just their balance. 10. Flag any matter below the trust threshold the same day. Not at the next billing cycle. The same day. A delay means the client's case could stall without warning. 11. Process Invoices the Right Way 12. Prepare, review, and distribute client invoices on a biweekly cycle, so clients receive accurate, consistent billing they can follow. 13. Review every time entry on every invoice for accuracy, specificity, and consistency. Flag entries that are vague, duplicative, or do not reflect the actual work performed, because a confusing invoice erodes the client's trust in the firm. 15. Contact timekeepers directly to resolve questionable entries before pre-bills go to attorneys. The client should never have to question whether an entry is real. 17. Distribute finalized invoices on the scheduled date with payment links included so clients always know what they owe and how to pay without chasing anyone down. 18. Collect by Connecting Payment to Progress 19. Maintain accounts receivable below 2% of total billings. 20. Execute 12-15 outbound calls per day during the morning AR block, with every call documented in Clio so the client's history is always current if another tea ---------- mber needs to step in. 21. Lead every collections conversation with a case update: what was accomplished, what is upcoming, and how the work connects to the client's goal. The client hears the value before they hear the number. 22. When a client says they cannot pay, walk through every option: credit cards, personal loans, family support, employer assistance, and legal fee financing. You do not accept "I cannot" without helping them look at every door first, because a client who feels they have no options may abandon a case they still need. 23. Send payment links the same day after any commitment so the client can act while the conversation is fresh. 24. Listen, Learn, and Report What Clients Need Pay attention to what clients tell you on every call. Their questions, their frustrations, their confusion, and their feedback are data the firm needs to hear so we can serve them better. 25. Produce a weekly deliverable every Friday, capturing client feedback, recurring questions, unresolved needs, and what you are hearing about the client experience. This is how the firm stays connected to what clients actually need instead of guessing. 26. When a billing concern arises, log it with a documented timestamp and route it to the responsible attorney via email so the client gets a response, not silence. 27. Escalate any concern involving bar grievance, fraud, or legal action language to firm leadership the same day, because those situations require immediate attention to protect the client and the firm. 28. Stay Ahead of the Attorneys Check attorney calendars for upcoming hearings, mediations, and trials. Initiate additional retainer requests before anyone asks, so the client has time to prepare instead of scrambling. 29. Confirm all credits, write-offs, and billing holds in writing before any related bill is finalized. If a credit is pending and you are not certain it has been applied, hold the bill. A client should never receive an invoice that does not reflect what the firm already knows. 30. Document every retainer reduction, billing pause, or special instruction in Clio at the matter level the same day so the next person who touches the file has the full picture and the client never has to repeat themselves. Qualifications Required: • 2+ years in billing, collections, or accounts receivable in a professional services environment. Law firm experience strongly preferred. • High comfort with outbound phone calls and client-facing conversations. This role requires 20+ calls per day. If phones drain you, this is not the right fit. • Proficiency with practice management software (Clio Manage preferred, or ability to learn within 30 days). • Ability to read and interpret legal invoices, time entries, trust account statements, and engagement agreements. • Strong written communication for documented escalations, client correspondence, and weekly deliverables. • Proficiency with Google Workspace (Gmail, Sheets, Calendar, Drive). • Demonstrated ability to manage 100+ active relationships simultaneously without dropping threads. Preferred • Experience in a family law firm or litigation practice. • Familiarity with the Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct as they relate to billing. Training provided, but baseline awareness accelerates onboarding. • Experience with evergreen retainer models and trust accounting. • Prior use of LawPay, Dialpad, or Clio Grow. • Bilingual (English/Spanish) is a plus. About Divorce with a Plan Benefits / Why Work Here • Fully remote. We serve clients across the entire state of Maryland. You work from wherever you work best. • A firm that builds systems so clients get a consistent experience. You will have scripts, checklists, escalation protocols, a daily structure, and technology supporting you from day one. • Direct impact you can measure. Your collections rate, your AR percentage, the client feedback you surface: you will see exactly how your work makes a difference for real people going through real situations. • Training on the Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct as they apply to billing. This gives you compliance knowledge that transfers to any law firm career and ensures every client interaction meets the standard. How to Apply • Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your legal billing experience, familiarity with trust accounting, and any experience with Clio or similar platforms. Bilingual candidates are encouraged to note their language proficiency. • As part of the application process, please also complete the initial interview using the link below: • Initial AI Interview Link: ---------- • Applications that include both a resume and completed initial interview will be prioritized.

description: ClickUp Expert – Workflow & Best Practices Consultant Type: Project-Based Gig | Independent Contractor Project Length: 3 weeks (fixed timeline) Pay Structure: Fixed project price, paid out in milestones upon completion of agreed deliverables Location: Remote | (U.S. Eastern Time availability preferred for live working sessions) Engagement: Defined-scope consulting project with potential for ongoing retainer support after completion About ---------- ---------- is a leading provider of business book summaries, delivering professional, high-quality insights in text and audio formats. Documentation, Training & Handoff • Document the workspace structure, conventions, and “how we work in ClickUp” so the team has a clear reference. • Lead live training sessions (recorded) for tea ---------- mbers and managers. • Provide a clean handoff package so our team can confidently operate the system independently. description: For the website: ---------- Correct the following things: 1. Homepage structure 2. Flow Refinement 3. Call to Action (B.O.T. integration/Interactive A.I. B.O.T. implementation)[I have an avatar in mind for use here. 4. Call to action placements 5. Layout Spacing 6. Visual Hierarchy 7. Cleanup*[this refers to section A below] 8. Section A: **Audit Summary** I inspected [ ---------- ]( ---------- ), its shop pages, sitemap/robots files, rendered homepage structure, mobile layout behavior, and the visible A.I. chat widget. Short version: the brand/world is distinctive, but the site is currently carrying too much navigation, too many competing paths, weak mobile containment, uneven SEO structure, and unclear conversion priority. Those issues should be cleaned up before TikTok Shop integration, because TikTok traffic will be mostly mobile, fast-moving, and conversion-sensitive. [Creation of the TikTok store will be another gig/job] **Highest Priority Findings** 1. **Mobile friendliness needs urgent refinement** The homepage does not fit cleanly into a phone-width viewport. In a 390px mobile test, desktop-style navigation and CTA elements extended far off-screen, creating horizontal overflow. This is the biggest practical issue because TikTok Shop traffic will likely arrive from mobile/in-app browsing. 2. **Navigation is too deep** The homepage exposed about **70 links/ 65 unique URLs**, including many character, universe, community, group, member, and forum. This needs to not be deleted but repurposed to not be this "deep", , but cleaner and then leading to the depth in a more smooth fashion. shop, and dynamic pages. This weakens visitor decision-making. Recommended top-level nav: ·Home'·,Universe','Books','Shop', ·Characters·, ·Community'·,Contact'. Everything else should sit under structured hub pages. 3. **Homepage hierarchy is confused** The page has multiple'H1' elements: "ALL About The Author," "Enter The UnderShadow Universe," and duplicate "Enter The UnderShadow Agency Mall." The actual first-screen brand/title is marked as' H2', not 'H1•. This hurts accessibility, SEO clarity, and conversion flow. The homepage should have one primary'H1', likely "The UnderShadow Agency," with secondary sections beneath it. 4. **CTA flow is visually present but strategically unclear** There are CTAs for Shop, About, Mall, subscription, contact, and A.I. chat, but the page does not make one primary next action obvious. For TikTok Shop readiness, the site should prioritize: 'Watch/Discover-> Shop featured item-> Join briefing list-> Ask C.O.S.M.O.S./B.O.T.' Right now those actions compete rather than guide. 5. **B.O.T./A.I. chat is present, but response reliability needs review** The "Chat with Al" widget opened successfully and displayed a welcome response. I tested a simple query: "Where can I buy books or merch?" The message appeared in the chat, but I did not observe a follow-up A.I. answer during the test window. That should be retested inside the site/admin tooling because the front-end trigger works, but the response flow may need tuning. 6. **Performance risk is high** The rendered homepage showed about **155 observed assets**, including roughly **100 scripts**, **21 images**, **7 fonts**, **2 stylesheets**, and **1 video asset**. Wix handles some optimization automatically, including AVIF image delivery, but this is still heavy. Adding TikTok pixels, product embeds, automation scripts, or richer bot behavior without cleanup may worsen mobile load and responsiveness. 7. **Accessibility and image metadata need cleanup** On the homepage, I found **26 images** with **10 missing alt attributes**. On the APEX merch page, **18 images** with **9 missing alt attributes**. This affects accessibility, SEO, and product discoverability. 8. **Shop/CRO readiness is incomplete** The [Book Shop]( ---------- ) page has a weak meta description: "Book Shop." The [APEX merch page] ( ---------- ) has no visible heading structure detected and no meta description. Product listings are present, but the commerce path'i).eeds stronger product storytelling, trust cues, shipping/return clarity, reviews/social proof, and direct "Buy now" behavior. 9. **Product sitemap appears stale** The [store product sitemap]( ---------- ) lists products last modified in **2021**, while the page sitemap shows many pages updated around **May 19, 2026**. Before TikTok Shop, product metadata should be refreshed: titles, descriptions, images, availability, pricing, canonical URLs, and structured product data where possible. 10. **SEO indexability is mostly open, but sitemap structure is noisy** The [robots.txt]( ---------- ) allows crawling and points to sitemaps. The [main sitemap]( ---------- . ---------- /sitemap.xml) includes many multilingual and dynamic sitemap entries. That is not inherently bad, but it increases the need for clean carionical strategy, correct page titles, and no thin/duplicate dynamic pages. **Additional Categories To Add** - **Accessibility/WCAG:** heading order, alt text, keyboard navigation, contrast, form labels, chat accessibility. - **SEO governance:** page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, duplicate "copy-of' URLs, product schema. - **Commerce trust:** shipping, returns, delivery time, payment methods, product size/fit info, reviews. - **TikTok Shop readiness:** mobile product landing pages, pixel/events, UTM tracking, product feed quality, creator/social proof. - **Content architecture:** separate "world-building" from "buy/subscribe" paths so visitors are not asked to decode the universe before converting. - **Automation QA:** verify chat scripts, form submissions, newsletter automations, abandoned cart, TikTok event firing, and CRM tagging from admin/testing tools.

title: Project / Studio Manager (Design Agency)
description: Anyday is a product-design subscription studio. Funded startups and scaling teams pay us a flat monthly fee and get a senior design team on tap — no scoping wars, no per-project haggling, no hiring a $300k Head of Design. We design the products people actually use: fintech apps, banking flows, payments platforms, SaaS tools. We're small, fast, and profitable. We run lean on a senior contractor model, we ship weekly, and we punch well above our size because we're systemised, not chaotic. Our clients stay because the work is good and because working with us is easy — and that second part is the job we're hiring for. What we do - Product design — app and web-app UI/UX for funded startups. - Brand & web — identity systems and marketing sites alongside the product work. - AI & automation — workflow audits and AI-assisted tools built into client products and our own ops. We deliver through a small bench of senior designers, a fractional Head of Design (our founder), and tight, AI-augmented operations. You'd be the person who keeps that machine humming. Why this role matters Right now the founder is the bottleneck — he sells, designs, and runs every project. The studio is growing faster than one person can traffic. This role takes the entire delivery engine off his plate. That means you're not a note-taker or a status-chaser. You run the studio floor. You decide who works on what, you protect the client relationship, and you're the reason a client opens Slack on Monday already knowing exactly where their project stands. Get this right and you become the operational backbone of a studio that's about to scale across multiple brands — with the autonomy and ownership that comes with being early. We lean hard on AI to do this well. If you already use AI to summarise calls, draft status updates, triage requests, and move faster than a "normal" PM - you'll feel at home and you'll have room to build the system further. What you'll do - Traffic the studio — assign and balance design work across clients and designers so nothing slips and no one's overloaded. - Own client communication — run a weekly Monday status update for every active client so they always know what's shipping, what's next, and what you need from them. Kill the mid-week "any update?" pings before they happen. - Drive projects to done — track every deliverable in ClickUp against quoted scope; flag risks early; keep delivery on time and on brief. - Guard profitability — track logged hours against quoted scope and surface overruns before they eat margin. - Onboard new clients — set expectations, stand up channels, and get the first deliverable moving cleanly. - Run our ops with AI — use AI tools to summarise calls, draft updates, triage requests, and tighten the delivery system over time. - Keep the pipeline honest — maintain the proposal / project tracker (win rates, follow-ups, engagement) so we learn from every deal. Must-haves - Project / studio / traffic management experience — ideally at a design, creative, or digital agency. - Excellent English communication — you'll be the client's main point of contact, written and on calls. - Genuinely organised — you keep many moving projects clear in your head and in the tools. - Tool fluency — ClickUp (or similar PM tools), Slack, and a real appetite for AI tools to work faster. - Calm under load — comfortable juggling competing priorities without dropping balls. - UAE / GST working-hours overlap for client calls and daily traffic. Nice-to-haves - Design or creative background (you don't design, but you should speak the language). - FinTech / SaaS client exposure. - Experience building or improving delivery systems and SOPs, not just running them. - Comfort being early at a fast-scaling, multi-brand studio. Engagement - Type: Part-time contractor to start, scaling toward full-time as client load grows. - Hours: ~20 hrs/week to begin, flexible. Daily presence matters more than block hours — the studio needs eyes on it every working day. - Reporting: Works directly with the founder (fractional Head of Design); partners closely with the senior designers. - Tools: ClickUp, Slack, Figma (viewing), plus our AI stack.

title: Senior UI / UX Designer
description: Senior UI/UX designer embedded with a design agencies new and growing clients. You own product design end-to-end — research, flows, UI, design systems — and you front it directly with the client on calls. This is not a "take the brief, go quiet, deliver pixels" role. You think alongside the founder, defend your decisions, and lift the quality bar for the whole team. The work mixes FinTech and funded SaaS — payments, banking, financial products. Recent and pipeline clients include a digital-banking AI project, a payments platform, and fintech custody tooling. Comfort with regulated, trust-heavy, data-dense interfaces matters. What you'll do - Lead product design for Anyday's newest clients — own the work from problem to shipped UI. - Run client calls: present concepts, walk through flows, take feedback live, and steer the conversation. - Defend and present your ideas — explain the "why" behind a decision and hold the line when it's right. - Produce high-craft UX: user flows, wireframes, prototypes, polished UI, and design-system upkeep in Figma. - Collaborate async day-to-day (Slack), with steady weekly delivery. - Set the quality standard juniors can follow (mentoring is a plus, not required day one). Must-haves - Figma — expert. This is the daily tool, no exceptions. - FinTech experience — shipped work for financial, banking, payments, or regulated products. - Strong English communication — written and spoken, clear and confident. - Comfortable on calls — client-facing, not behind-the-scenes only. - Defends and presents ideas well — can justify design decisions and respond to pushback in real time. - Senior-level UX skills — research-to-flow-to-UI, not just visual execution. - Reliable overlap with UAE / GST working hours for client calls. Engagement - Type: Full-time contractor. - Hours: ~110 hrs/month (? 5 hrs/day × 22 working days) to start, with room to grow to full-time. - Reporting: Works directly with Nathan (founder) and the traffic manager once that role is filled. - Tools: Figma, Slack, ClickUp. Want to see the thinking (flows, decisions), not just final screens. - Confirmation of working-hours overlap with UAE time.

title: Website Project Manager
description: Web Project Manager: Full Time An exciting opportunity exists for a Project Manager in the online marketing and website design industry. This position is suited to someone who loves organising and interacting with clients. From client onboarding, setting them up in our project management system, to sending the briefing questionnaires, collating their responses and information for the website project. To oversight on the design, managing the actual build, then to client preview, to the final site go live process. Project Management requires high attention to detail. That starts NOW, if you can't follow the job ad process then you will automatically exclude your application from consideration. Must have a reliable internet connection and good PC. MUST know WordPress (not just how to spell it). Must understand website design. NOTE: Please submit a voice recording explaining why you are the best person for the job. =============================================================================== Remuneration by agreement • Permanent Basis (long term) • 40 hours per week • Rapidly growing company (Lots of work on its books) The company is situated in Perth, Western Australia (So same time zone as the Philippines). MUSTS: • Good spoken English • Good written English =============================================================================== Customer Service & Admin Support • Customer Support • Email Support • Phone Support Project Management • Design Project Management • Web Development Project Management =============================================================================== We build websites, from business start-ups to sophisticated high level websites. We also do SEO, social media, copywriting, and most things digital marketing or website related. Website project management is a high attention to detail role. You cannot fake attention to detail, you either have it, or you don’t. Don’t waste your time or ours if that’s not you. From when a new client comes on board, to the briefing, data collation and tracking, guidance with the client for the layout and website functionality, and then through to design concepts, and then onto tasking and liaising with the design and build team for the actual build and implementation. This is a marketing ideas role, and a communication role requiring good interpersonal skills. EG: In a recent simple project the client had 3 primary services, hats, shirts and badges. In the design layout and function briefing it was d ---------- we were to create 3 primary ‘doorway’ buttons on one row on the homepage linking to those product pages. The client then requested a 4th button to showcase suppliers. We could do that, add a 4th button on that one row, no problems. But, was that a good marketing or design decision? Was it going to be in the client’s best interest? Should that page have the same priority as the 3 main product pages? What would your response have been to that client’s request? We have broken the website build process into 10 distinct stages, from project setup and client onboarding right through to design and build and onto quality assurance, a clear ‘go live’ process and handover steps to project completion rap up. There are 560 specific steps in this process, and it’s the project managers role to make sure they’re all adhered to in their fullness but a timely manner to deliver a high-end product. Software we use: • Teamwork: For client communication, project management, time tracking. • Zoom • Slack for team comms • WHMCS for client support • Process St for ALL processes and systems • Trello for tasking • RoboForm for password management • OneDrive for all file assets What does your day look like? • Morning check in – Daily Focus session • Check email s for project notifications, respond • Follow up with clients • Follow up with team, and check tasks previously assigned • Ensure that new project tasks are assigned to team • Liaise with clients • Handle brief questionnaires with clients • Handle layout and function briefings with clients • Check off that process has been adhered to • Manage team and resources Here’s the question: Can you see your existing skills sets being suited to these daily tasks? We have a local tech, who handles the phones, helps in support and also does our SEO. We have another local tech, who handles the hosting, website version updates, managed support and all things WordPress for clients. We have several designers and web build dev’s who handles the design concepts, and the actual build as such. We also have a remote marketing person, who is our CRM specialist on the team. There is also a content marketing and social media specialist. So, is that you? Remember, don’t theorise about this! Website project management is a high attention to detail role. You cannot fake attention to detail, you either have it, or you don’t. Don’t waste your time or ours if that’s not you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO (TRAINING PROVIDED) * Log into Windows virtual machines via remote desktop every day and check that they are running correctly. * Monitor automated betting software on each VM - confirm sessions are active, bookmakers are logged in, and there are no errors. * On Saturdays and busy race days, check VMs more frequently to catch bookmakers that log out mid-session. * Fix common issues - restart frozen VMs, re-log bookmaker accounts, restart betting software sessions. * Escalate infrastructure-level problems (proxy connections, VPN, server issues) to the technical support team. * Maintain accurate tracking records - account balances, VM statuses, and operational data. * Sign up to new bookmaker accounts as instructed, following the exact process provided. * Provide daily updates to the owner on the state of the operation. NICE TO HAVE * Prior experience in betting operations, matched betting, or bookmaker account management. * Experience with automated betting tools. * Experience using Airtable or similar tracking tools. * Experience with remote desktop tools (RDM, AnyDesk, TeamViewer). SCHEDULE * Full-time, 40 hours per week. * Wednesday to Sunday, 8 hours per day. * Weekdays: 11:00am to 7:00pm AEST. * Saturdays: 9:00am start. * Australian timezone (AEST/AEDT). title: Supply & Inventory Managment
description: Supply & Inventory Management Manager Overview We are looking for an experienced Supply & Inventory Management Manager to take ownership of stock across a group of companies operating from multiple locations. This is a central, cross-functional role responsible for ensuring the right products are in the right place at the right time, across both physical warehouses and online marketplaces. You will sit at the heart of our operations, working across several ERP systems and sales channels to forecast demand, manage replenishment, control stock levels, and keep data accurate and reconciled across the group. Your decisions will directly drive availability, cash flow, and profitability, while reducing overstock, stockouts, and tied-up capital. This role suits someone who is highly numerate, systems-literate, and comfortable holding the bigger picture across multiple entities while also getting into the detail of individual SKUs, lead times, and supplier performance. Key Responsibilities Group-Wide Inventory Oversight Take overall responsibility for inventory across multiple companies, brands, and physical locations within the group. Maintain a single, reliable view of stock across all entities, reconciling discrepancies between systems, warehouses, and sales channels. Set and maintain minimum and maximum stock levels, safety stock, and reorder points for each location and channel. Implement consistent stock control processes, cycle counts, and stock takes across all sites. Demand Forecasting & Planning Forecast demand at SKU, channel, and location level using historical sales data, seasonality, promotions, and market trends. Factor in product lead times, supplier reliability, and manufacturing or shipping windows when planning purchasing and replenishment. Balance availability against working capital, avoiding both stockouts and excess holding. Plan ahead for peak periods, new product launches, and promotional activity across the group. ERP Systems & Data Management Manage and coordinate inventory data across multiple ERP systems used by different companies in the group. Ensure stock, purchasing, and sales data is accurate, consistent, and synchronised between systems and channels. Identify opportunities to standardise, integrate, or improve ERP and inventory workflows across the group. Act as a key point of contact for system data integrity, troubleshooting mismatches and driving process improvement. Marketplace & Online Channel Coordination Oversee inventory allocation and synchronisation across online marketplaces such as Amazon, Shopify, and TikTok Shop. Ensure stock is correctly distributed and listed across channels to maximise availability and sales without overselling. Coordinate with fulfilment and channel teams to align listings, stock feeds, and replenishment with demand. Monitor channel performance and adjust allocation strategies to protect margins and service levels. Replenishment & Lead Time Management Own the end-to-end replenishment process, raising and managing purchase orders in line with demand and lead times. Track inbound stock, follow up on overdue deliveries, and manage exceptions such as delays, shortages, or damaged goods. Continuously review supplier lead times and reliability, feeding this into planning and reorder logic. Supplier, 3PL & Warehouse Coordination Act as the main point of contact between suppliers, prep centres, and 3PL/warehouse partners across locations. Coordinate shipment schedules, inbound bookings, and stock transfers between sites and entities. Manage returns, damaged or missing goods, and associated supplier claims or refunds. Build strong working relationships with suppliers to improve terms, reliability, and responsiveness. Reporting & Analysis Develop and maintain key reporting on stock levels, stock value, turnover, ageing, availability, and forecast accuracy. Provide clear, regular reporting to leadership on inventory health and risks across the group. Use data to identify slow-moving and dead stock, recommend actions, and continuously improve inventory efficiency. Track and report on key metrics such as stock turn, sell-through, fill rate, and days of cover. Required Skills & Qualifications Minimum 2-3 years of hands-on experience in inventory, supply chain, or stock management, ideally across multiple locations or entities. Proven experience working with ERP and inventory management systems, including reconciling data across more than one platform. Strong demand forecasting and planning skills, with a solid grasp of lead times, reorder logic, and safety stock. Highly numerate and analytical, comfortable working with large datasets and turning them into clear decisions. Advanced spreadsheet skills (Excel/Sheets) and confidence with reporting and data tools. Experience managing inventory across online marketplaces such as Amazon, Shopify, or TikTok Shop. Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities across companies and locations. Strong communication and coordination skills, comfortable liaising with suppliers, 3PLs, and internal teams. Desirable Skills Experience working across a group structure with several companies, brands, or trading entities. Familiarity with multiple ERP systems and an understanding of how to integrate or standardise them. Knowledge of 3PL and prep centre operations. Experience with multichannel inventory or listing tools that sync stock across marketplaces. Understanding of cash flow and working capital implications of inventory decisions. A continuous-improvement mindset, with the ability to streamline processes and systems. Benefits Central, high-impact role with visibility across the whole group. Opportunity to shape inventory and supply processes across multiple companies and channels. Fast-paced, growing business with real ownership and autonomy. Ongoing professional development and growth opportunities. This position is ideal for someone who is organised, data-driven, and confident managing complexity across multiple companies, systems, and sales channels. If you enjoy bringing order to moving parts and using data to keep a growing operation stocked, efficient, and profitable, this role offers a challenging and rewarding opportunity.

title: Design Operations Specialist (Production Designer)
description: Design Operations Specialist (Production Designer) The short version We're not looking for an artist. AI tools now handle a lot of the "make it look good" work. We're looking for someone who can own the design process end-to-end — take a brief, run with it, talk to suppliers directly, get production-ready files out the door, and not need to be chased or supervised at every step. If you read a request and your instinct is "got it, I'll handle it and come back when it's done" — keep reading. If your instinct is to send it back for approval before acting, this isn't the role. What you'll actually do Take creative direction and turn it into production-ready artwork and assets across multiple product lines (printed, laser-cut, packaging, catalogues, product mockups). Drive AI design tools (e.g. Recraft and GPT) confidently — using them as your primary production engine, not as a novelty. Prepare and check files against manufacturing specs (print-ready files, DXF / cut files, dimensions, bleed, colour) and catch errors before they reach a supplier. Own supplier and client communication on artwork. When a supplier asks a question, you answer it directly and close the loop — you don't bounce it back up the chain. Manage the workflow: track what's in progress, what's waiting, what's done, and keep things moving without being prompted. Spot problems early and solve them, or flag them clearly with a recommended fix. Who you are You take ownership. "Please send this to the supplier" means you send it and handle their reply — not that you send it back to us first. You're analytical and detail-tight. You don't make the same mistake twice, and you check your own work before it goes out. You're comfortable with ambiguity. You ask sharp clarifying questions up front, then execute — you don't need hand-holding through every step. You're fluent (or fast-learning) with AI design tools and genuinely excited about working this way. You communicate clearly in writing — concise, complete, and proactive. No one-word replies that leave us guessing. What matters more than a fine-art degree A background in production, manufacturing, retail operations, or project/product workflow management is more valuable to us than a traditional graphic design or fine-art portfolio. We want systems thinking applied to design — someone who sees the whole pipeline, not just the pretty picture. Strong technical execution still matters (clean, accurate, professional output), but raw artistic flair is the least important thing on this list. How to apply Send your portfolio and a short answer to these two questions: Describe a time you were given an unclear or incomplete brief. What did you do? A supplier replies to artwork you sent with a technical question you're not 100% sure how to answer. Walk us through exactly what you do next. We read the answers to these before we look at anything else.

title: Operations & Project Manager (Fast Growing)
description: This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos - Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company. - Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics. - Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. - Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves! If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace. Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days) We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Eight years later he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full?time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass?applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth Comp: Starting base $600–$700, with performance bonuses that take you to $900+ when you consistently hit + beat KPIs.” Raises and benefits are tied directly to beating KPIs, & raising the standard, not time served If you crush it, scope grows into higher-level ops ownership and comp follows output The Filipino teammate in the story above is now at ~$2,500/month and on the way up (and your growth trajectory will be much faster if you earn it because of strong systems, much better leadership, and I know what the fuck we’re doing). There is no ceiling here, this is not a forever $800 grind. But you have to earn it. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. How To Apply (24-Hour Test) Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises) If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are: A short interview focused on your past execution. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each. Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders. Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list): – “Fix Asana, it’s a mess” – “Seller lead texting follow up??” – “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ” – “Inventory backlog insane” – “Need better reporting” – “Update SOPs In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager. In a Google Doc, please: Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points. Link the Google Doc here (view access). Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying. Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link. Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here.

Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Eight years later he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full?time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass?applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth • Ramp: $600 base while you’re learning the systems (first 30–90 days). • Once you’re hitting KPI floors, expected OTE = $800–$1,000/month (base + performance bonus). • Raises and benefits are tied directly to beating KPIs & raising the standard, not time served. • If you crush it, scope grows into higher-level ops ownership and comp follows output. The Filipino teammate in the story above is now at ~$2,500/month and climbing. This is not a forever $800 grind, but you have to earn it. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Q4: Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list): – “Fix Asana, it’s a mess” – “Seller lead texting follow up??” – “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ” – “Inventory backlog insane” – “Need better reporting” – “Update SOPs In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager. description: Full-time Court Portal Researcher Remote | Full time | $2.00–$2.75/hr USD depending on experience About the role We are a fast-growing document preparation company that monitors public court records across the United States. We need a sharp, fast, and reliable full-time researcher whose only job is finding and documenting US court portals that meet our criteria. This is a focused role. You are not building scrapers. You are not entering data. You are researching websites, testing them against a clear checklist, documenting your findings, and delivering results every single day. Speed and accuracy matter equally here. What you will do Visit US county court portal websites across multiple states and test each one against our four criteria checklist. For every portal document the following in our shared Google Sheet: — Portal URL — Whether results can be filtered by filing date without entering a name — yes or no — Whether the defendant or tenant name is visible in search results — yes or no — Whether the property address is visible in search results — yes or no — Whether there is a login wall, CAPTCHA, or paywall blocking access — yes or no — Estimated weekly filing volume based on visible results — Your classification — Green, Yellow, or Red — Screenshot or link as evidence Green means all four criteria are met and a scraper can be built immediately. Yellow means most criteria are met but something is missing — usually the address. Red means the portal is blocked, requires login, or is legally restricted. Deliver a minimum of 5 to 8 fully documented portal assessments per day. Every row must be complete. No blanks. No guessing. If you are unsure classify it as unclear and note why. What we are looking for Fast and systematic — you work through portals methodically without getting stuck Detail oriented — every field filled in accurately every time Reliable — you show up every day Monday through Friday and communicate proactively Comfortable navigating US government and court websites Good written English for clear notes and updates Stable internet connection What we are NOT looking for Someone who researches 2 portals a day and calls it done Someone who submits incomplete rows Someone who disappears without notice Someone who needs constant supervision Hours and pay Full time — 40 hours per week — Monday through Friday $2.00 to $2.75 per hour depending on speed and accuracy First 30 days probation — rate confirmed at hire Paid twice a month on the 1st and 15th via Wise or PayPal How to apply Send your application to ---------- Subject line: Court Portal Researcher Application Include: 1. Your experience with online research and data documentation 2. Confirm you are available full time Monday through Friday 3. Confirm stable internet connection 4. Your expected hourly rate within the range above 5. Answer this question in 2 to 3 sentences: You need to find out if a county court website allows you to search eviction cases by filing date without entering any names. Walk us through exactly how you would test that.

job_title: AI Video + VFX + Real Scene Producer Needed for Premium Brand Videos
description: Comment to "Type of Employment: Any": This starts as two Gigs, but can turn into a long Full-Time job. Now to the JOB DESCRIPTION: Project: two Videos (Short Clips) One will need AI and VFX skills. The other is some real-life filming and IA skills. We are looking for a highly capable video creator or a small production team for two separate CruiseLife brand videos. These are not simple Canva videos, not slideshow videos, and not stock-footage-only projects. We need someone who can realistically judge what is possible with AI video, VFX, animation, stock material, and real filming — and then produce a professional final result. You may apply for Video 1 only, Video 2 only, or both videos, but please be very clear about what you can actually deliver. ________________________________________ Project 1: “The CruiseLife WAVE” This video requires a cinematic beach scene where a wave transforms into the CruiseLife wordmark. The key visual idea: A bright, sunny, elegant beach scene. A wave rolls toward the viewer. The water gradually forms abstract shapes, then hints of upside-down letters, then rotates into upright letters, and finally, the word CruiseLife lands deeply in the wet sand as a large 3D wordmark. This project requires: • Strong VFX / animation capability • Water simulation or convincing AI/VFX water effects • 3D text/wordmark integration • Realistic interaction between wave, sand, splash, droplets, and letters • Ability to follow a detailed storyboard • Ability to avoid side-view mistakes, mirrored letters, or generic wave footage • Final output suitable for brand marketing Important: This project previously failed because the freelancer could edit video but could not deliver the required VFX. Please do not apply for this project unless you can show real examples of comparable VFX, water effects, 3D text integration, or advanced AI/VFX work. ________________________________________ Project 2: CruiseLife USP Video This is a brand / USP video explaining the emotional and commercial idea behind CruiseLife. The video will probably combine: • AI-generated scenes • Stock footage where suitable • Motion graphics • Text overlays • Voice-over and music • Possibly a few scenes with real people Important: This project previously failed because the available AI/stock material was not enough. Some scenes may require real human performance, lifestyle shots, or staged scenes with people. Therefore, we need someone who can either: 1. Personally film simple scenes with real people, or 2. Organize/direct such filming, or 3. Clearly explain which scenes can be created with AI and which scenes must be filmed. Please do not apply if your only method is downloading stock clips and putting text on top. ________________________________________ What We Need From You Please apply only if you can provide: • A realistic production plan • Honest assessment of what can be done with AI, VFX, stock footage, and real filming • Strong English communication • Ability to work from a detailed storyboard/script • Regular progress updates • Short preview clips before final rendering • Clean final export in high quality • Commercial usage rights for all footage, music, voice, AI output, and edited material ________________________________________ Required Application Details Please answer these questions in your application: 1. Are you applying for Video 1, Video 2, or both? 2. Which tools do you use? Example: Runway, Kling, Veo, Midjourney, After Effects, Blender, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, etc. 3. For Video 1: Can you create realistic VFX involving waves, water, sand, splash, and 3D text? Please show examples. 4. For Video 2: Can you film or organize simple scenes with real people if AI/stock footage is not enough? 5. Please send 3–5 examples of your best relevant work. 6. What exactly did you personally do in those examples? 7. Are you comfortable working from a very detailed storyboard and following exact visual instructions? 8. What would be your recommended workflow for this type of project? 9. What is your estimated price range for a 30–60 second video of this quality? 10. How many revisions are included? ________________________________________ Important Quality Requirement We are not looking for someone who simply says, “Yes, I can do it.” We are looking for someone who can say: • “This part is possible with AI.” • “This part needs VFX.” • “This part should be filmed.” • “This part is risky.” • “This is the best workflow.” • “Here is a small test before we continue.” Honesty and technical judgment are more important than overpromising. ________________________________________ First Step / Test Before awarding the full project, we may request a short paid test scene. For Video 1, this could be a 5–10 second sample showing wave / water / 3D wordmark integration. For Video 2, this could be a 10–15 second sample scene showing the intended style, pacing, stock/AI/filmed material approach, and overall brand feeling. ________________________________________ Brand Context CruiseLife is a lifestyle and fashion brand. The tone should be: • Positive • Sunny • Elegant • Emotional • Aspirational • Premium but not arrogant • Suitable for international marketing The goal is to create video content that feels like a real brand campaign, not like a cheap AI experiment. ________________________________________ Please Do Not Apply If • You only create basic AI videos without editing skill • You only use stock footage • You cannot do or coordinate VFX • You cannot follow a detailed storyboard • You cannot communicate clearly in English • You cannot show relevant examples • You are not comfortable doing a small test first ________________________________________ Final Deliverables Final deliverables should include: • Final video file in high quality • Version suitable for website / social media • Project files if agreed • Source assets where legally possible • Confirmation that all materials are cleared for commercial use

title: Operations & Project Manager (Fast Growing)
description: Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal. What You Get If You Win Here - High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos - Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company. - Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics. - Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. - Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves! If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace. Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days) We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth (All of this is written into your contract.) Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial • $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit. • No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors. Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside • Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward. • On top of base, you can earn: $400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them). $1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard. • In practice, that means: Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month All bonuses are 100% KPI based  (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture. Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay) We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat. We also protect uninterrupted deep?work blocks for you every week (no rando ---------- etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back?to?back Zoom calls. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. How To Apply (24-Hour Test) Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises) If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are: A short interview focused on your past execution. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each. Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders. Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list): – “Fix Asana, it’s a mess” – “Seller lead texting follow up??” – “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ” – “Inventory backlog insane” – “Need better reporting” – “Update SOPs In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager. In a Google Doc, please: Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points. Link the Google Doc here (view access). Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying. Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link. Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here.
