title: Backlink & AI Visibility Specialist
description: DON'T APPLY IF >>>>> Please read carefully. We would like applicants to have tests, IQ and identity above 80%. Also please submit your best samples as they are factored for alignment with our quality. Backlink & AI Visibility Specialist (SEO · AEO · GEO) We're a digital marketing agency specializing in trades and construction businesses, and we're hiring a Backlink & AI Visibility Specialist to build and grow off-page authority for our own brand and our clients' brands — and to make sure those brands are accurately cited and surfaced by AI-powered search engines, large language models (LLMs), and answer engines. This is a hybrid role that bridges traditional link building with two emerging disciplines: Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). You'll work across multiple client accounts, so you should already have a vetted list of backlink sources and placements you've personally used with success. Experience: 2–5 years in link building or SEO Employment type: Full-time (contract options available) Focus areas: Link building + AEO/GEO + AI search & LLM citation Core link-building responsibilities Research and prospect link targets using Ahrefs, Semrush, and Moz — but prioritize niche relevance and real editorial traffic over raw DA/DR scores. A relevant link from a trade publication beats twenty links from high-authority sites no one reads Run journalist-source and digital-PR outreach (email , LinkedIn) using current platforms — Qwoted, Source of Sources (SOS), ---------- , and #JournoRequest on X (HARO/Connectively shut down in Dec 2024; don't rely on it) — to earn guest posts, editorial links, resource-page placements, and press coverage Conduct competitor backlink analysis to identify gaps and replicate genuinely earnable, high-value opportunities Monitor backlink profiles, identify toxic links, and submit disavow requests via Google Search Console Work with the content team to develop linkable assets — original data studies, surveys, infographics, and long-form guides that publishers actually want to cite Local citations & directory management Manually build and manage local citations and business directory listings across Canadian and North American platforms — the kind of work a tool like BrightLocal automates, done by hand for accuracy and full control Set up new accounts and complete listings from scratch where needed, keeping NAP (Name, Address, Phone) data consistent across every directory Work from a provided master list of target directories for manual entry, and proactively flag additional niche- or region-relevant directories worth adding Keep listings current over time — updating details, removing duplicates, and verifying entries AEO, GEO & LLM citation responsibilities Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Optimize content to be selected as the direct answer in Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Bing Copilot, Perplexity, voice assistants, and featured snippets Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): Ensure our brands, products, and content are accurately represented and cited in outputs from generative AI models including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Audit how — and whether — our brands are cited in LLM outputs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) and track citation frequency, accuracy, and sentiment over time Earn mentions and citations on the sources AI answer engines index most heavily — authoritative publications, industry wikis, Reddit, Quora, and reputable government/educational domains Note: many of these placements are "no-follow" and won't pass traditional link equity. For AEO/GEO that's expected — the goal is AI citation and entity strength, not PageRank. We want someone who understands that distinction. Structure content for extraction: lead with a direct 40–60 word answer block, use FAQ schema, speakable schema, and clear entity definitions, and write in an objective, declarative voice (AI engines down-weight "we think / in our opinion" hedging) Keep content fresh and specific — recency and concrete statistics are heavily weighted, especially by Perplexity, which refreshes near-daily and cites 4–8 sources per answer Make sure AI crawlers can actually read the page: critical text rendered server-side (not injected by client-side JavaScript), and the right crawler access configured (e.g. OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT search eligibility, distinct from GPTBot training access) Develop and execute digital PR strategies aimed at earning mentions on high-E-E-A-T domains that serve as training and retrieval sources for AI models Strengthen entity recognition across AI systems by optimizing Knowledge Panels, Wikidata entries, and third-party review platforms (G2, Trustpilot, Clutch) How we work — our standards (non-negotiables) Link building in 2026 is about earning citations and trust, not gaming volume. We expect you to: Earn, don't manipulate. No PBNs, link farms, paid link networks, comment spam, or scaled/automated link schemes. Google's spam updates penalize these, and one bad shortcut can damage a client account we've spent months building. Manually vet every target. Real editorial standards, real organic traffic, real topical relevance — not just a metric in a tool. Disclose paid placements with rel="sponsored" where applicable. Build relationships, not one-offs. Repeat publisher relationships beat cold-blasting templates that editors delete on sight. Honour the human edit pass. Any AI-assisted outreach or content draft gets a human voice + accuracy review before it goes out. Drafts are never sent or published raw. How we measure success This role is tracked against clear outputs, reviewed monthly. You'll work from a shared tracker (provided) and keep it current. Core KPIs: Links/citations earned — count, by type (editorial, guest, resource, directory, digital PR) and by client Quality of placements — relevance + real traffic, not just DR/DA Live link survival rate — placements that stay live and indexed Citation tracking (AEO/GEO): a monthly prompt audit — run 20–30 buyer-intent prompts per client across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, logging whether the brand is cited, citation accuracy, and sentiment over time Local citation health — directory listings live, NAP-consistent, duplicate-free Toxic-link monitoring — flagged and disavowed as needed Detailed recurring tasks, cadence, and tracking columns live in the accompanying VA task tracker. What we're looking for 2–5 years of hands-on link building or SEO experience A documented track record of placements you can show us (live URLs) Working knowledge of AEO/GEO is a strong plus; if you don't have it yet, you must be able to learn it fast Comfortable with high-volume, detail-accurate manual data entry — citation and directory work rewards consistency and care Honest grasp of what does and doesn't work — e.g., why self-placed Wikipedia links get reverted and how legitimate, policy-compliant entity presence is actually built Details Full-time, with contract options available pay range, weekly hours, and any time zone overlap you require] How to apply To be considered, your application must include: Your 3–5 best link-building or digital-PR samples — live URLs, each with a one-line note on why it mattered. Samples are weighted heavily; they're how we judge fit against our quality bar. ID Proof and IQ scores of 80% or higher on your profile

title: Head Of Operations
description: Why this role exists Right now every founder is trying to run their function AND keep the company organized. It is not working. Targets slip. Meetings happen without agendas. You will report to the CEO and have full authority to build processes, set cadence, and hold every department to its commitments. You are not here to do strategy. You are here to make strategy happen. What you will own Operating rhythm — across every department: • Run the Monday business standup (30 min, all leads, action items captured). • Run the Friday close-out (what shipped, what slipped, what's at risk). • Run a monthly business review with the founders — pre-read pack, agenda, decisions captured, follow-ups assigned. • Own the action item log for every meeting that matters. Surface red flags to the CEO within 24 hours of a metric crossing a threshold. Process design — across every department: • Build operating playbooks for the repeating processes that today are reinvented each time: install onboarding for a new partner, partner quarterly business review, hiring loop, sales handoff to engineering, RMA handling. • Document each process in plain language. Make it findable, followable, and updatable. • Roll process out one department at a time. • Audit adherence. If a process isn't being followed, find out why and either fix the process or escalate to the CEO. Project management: • Translate every CEO directive into a project plan with owner, deadline, dependencies, and milestone checkpoints. • Hold the named owner accountable. Escalate if they miss commits twice in a row. • Maintain the master project list. The CEO must be able to see at a glance what's in flight, what's at risk, what's overdue. OKR ownership: • Build the quarterly OKR cycle. Each function sets OKRs aligned to company goals. • Run quarterly OKR review with the founders. Score, learn, reset

description: Senior CATI Operations Manager — Remote, Market Research Employer: TKW Research Group (Australia / New Zealand) Location: Remote — Philippines (Metro Manila or Cebu preferred for talent network access) Engagement: Independent contractor, full-time equivalent The Package — What You’ll Receive TKW Research Group is a long-standing Australian/New Zealand market research firm, and we’re looking for a senior operations leader to take ownership of our CATI call floor — and to help shape what comes next. No middle layers. • Base retainer: ?130,000 – ?180,000 PHP per month, commensurate with seniority, paid in arrears. • 13th-month service bonus equivalent to one month’s base fee, paid every December. • HMO allowance of up to ?50,000 per year, fully reimbursing premium private health cover for you and one dependent. • Internet & equipment stipend of ?3,000 per month to support your home office setup. • 10 days of paid leave per annum after 12 months of service, plus observed Australian public holidays without reduction to your base fee. • Full training paid by TKW Research Group — structured onboarding plus ongoing dialler, CATI platform, and methodology training so you can perform at the highest level. • Real ownership of how the floor runs, working directly with senior ANZ leadership — no middle layers, no agency markup. You’ll be responsible for fieldwork execution, dialler performance, quota management, and the productivity of our interviewer teams. This is a senior, deeply hands-on role. You’ll have real autonomy over how the floor runs, but you’re also expected to roll up your sleeves — personally running shifts when needed and working directly with front-line interviewers, not just managing through layers. You’ll be accountable for hitting completion targets, maintaining quality, and keeping projects on budget. The Hybrid Future — What Makes This Different Every senior CATI manager knows what’s coming. Voicebots are going to reshape telephone interviewing within the next few years, and operations leaders fall into two camps: those who get sidelined by it, and those who lead the transition. We’re looking for the second kind. TKW Research Group is partnering with a tier-1 multinational AI platform provider to develop a survey voicebot — conversational AI that can conduct natural-sounding interviews at scale. Your role in this isn’t theoretical: as the voicebot moves from pilot to production, you’ll be the operational lead running the blended human/voicebot floor. D ---------- which interviews go to human interviewers and which go to the voicebot. Managing quality across both channels. Calibrating the hybrid model to deliver better data than either could alone. If you’ve been waiting for a CATI role where you get to shape what telephone research becomes — rather than manage its slow decline — this is it. What You’ll Do • Manage CATI fieldwork end-to-end: sample distribution, quota matrices, completion tracking. • Personally run live shifts when required — this is not a desk-only role. You’ll be on the floor (remotely) directing interviewers in real time, especially during critical fieldwork windows and across time zones. • Monitor dialler performance in real time — contact rates, call dispositions, interviewer yield — and make tactical calls to keep productivity up. • Coordinate Shift Supervisors, QA staff, and a remote interviewer pool. • Troubleshoot operational issues live and work directly with the survey programming team when scripts need adjustments. • Maintain ISO 20252 / ESOMAR-aligned quality processes. • Produce daily and weekly operational reporting for the COO. What We’re Looking For • 7+ years in CATI operations within a market research agency or fieldwork BPO, with 3+ years in a senior management role. • Strong working knowledge of dialler logic, CATI platforms, and call centre KPIs. • Genuinely good with front-line interviewers — you can motivate, coach, and direct base-level interviewers directly, not just manage through supervisors. The best candidates have come up through the floor and haven’t lost the common touch. • Solid grasp of market research methodology: sampling, quotas, weighting basics, and QA standards (ISO 20252, ESOMAR). • Forward-looking on AI in research — you don’t need technical AI experience, but you should see voicebots as an opportunity to lead, not a threat to manage around. • Comfortable with flexible shift patterns to cover multi-timezone fieldwork (agreed in advance — not random). • Home office with reliable power, dual internet connections, and a setup capable of running monitoring tools and video calls daily. • Strong written and spoken English. How to Apply Send your CV plus a short note covering: 1. The largest CATI operation you’ve personally run (team size, markets, sample volumes). 2. The dialler platforms you know best. 3. Your shift flexibility. 4. Your view on how voicebots will reshape telephone interviewing — and where you see your role in that shift.

title: UX/UI Web Designer
description: *Web Designer (UX/UI) — Gig / Part-time / Full-time* Boutique Branding Studio — Netherlands --- *About the Role* We're a boutique branding studio based in the Netherlands. We work at the intersection of brand strategy, identity, and digital execution. The websites we build are not afterthoughts to a brand project, they are the brand, made interactive. We're looking for a Web Designer who leads with structure and ends with craft. Someone who opens a new project by thinking about pages, flows, and systems, not colours and typefaces. The visual execution matters enormously, but it comes last. You'll join a small team on a gig basis, with a clear path to part-time and full-time for the right person. You'll own the design process from sitemap to hand-off, working alongside our brand leads and Webflow developer. --- *Who You Are* Before you are a designer, you are a systems thinker. You map information before you design screens. You wireframe to solve problems, not to sketch rough ideas. When you look at a website brief, your first instinct is to ask: what does this site need to do, how should it be structured, and how will someone move through it? You understand the web as a medium, not a canvas. You think about scroll behaviour, states, responsiveness, and hierarchy the way a developer thinks about logic: it either works or it doesn't. You're not a graphic designer who builds websites on the side. Web design is your specialism. It's where your thinking lives. --- *What You'll Do* — Translate briefs and brand strategy into sitemaps and content architecture before a single screen is designed — Build wireframes that define structure, hierarchy, and user flow with enough detail that they could be critiqued and approved on their own — Design full website concepts in Figma, desktop and mobile, using consistent components and a system-first approach — Build and maintain design systems and component libraries that scale across pages and projects — Hand off clean, structured Figma files to our Webflow developer with zero ambiguity — Work closely with brand leads from briefing through to final design, contributing to conceptual direction where needed --- *What We're Not Looking For* A graphic designer who can also do web. Someone who jumps to visual design before the structure is solved. Someone who designs pages in isolation without thinking about the system they belong to. Someone who needs direction at every step. If your portfolio is full of beautiful screens with no evidence of the thinking behind them, this is not the right role. --- *What We're Looking For* Required: — 5+ years specialising in web design — not general graphic, brand, or print design — A genuine process: sitemap ? wireframe ? visual design, every time — Strong information architecture skills — you can define page structure, navigation logic, and content hierarchy from a brief — Wireframes that stand on their own — detailed, annotated, and used as a real tool for alignment — Expert Figma skills: components, auto layout, variants, design systems, developer hand-off — A systems mindset — you think in reusable parts, not one-off pages — Deep understanding of web UX: conversion logic, scroll behaviour, mobile-first thinking, interactive states — Portfolio of live marketing and corporate websites that show process, not just output — Clear, proactive communicator in English Nice to have: — Familiarity with Webflow, knowing how your designs will be built makes you a better designer — Experience building or maintaining full design systems across multiple projects — Conceptual contribution to brand and campaign work that feeds into web — Micro-interaction or animation thinking at the wireframe stage --- *How We Work Together* A project starts with a briefing — sometimes strategic, sometimes a brand deep-dive, often both. From there, you lead: sitemap first, wireframes second, visual design third. You'll work closely with our brand leads and Webflow developer at each stage. Client communication stays with the studio. Your job is to design something that works and looks considered, then hand it off clearly. We're a small team. We don't micromanage, and we don't chase. We expect you to ask the right questions early, raise blockers when they appear, and deliver work that doesn't need explaining. --- *Compensation* Hourly rate is based on experience and portfolio. We pay well for the right person. This starts as a gig engagement. Strong collaborators will have the opportunity to move into a structured part-time role, and eventually a full-time position as the relationship grows. --- *How to Apply* Send us: — Your portfolio — live websites only. We're not interested in Dribbble shots, unsolicited redesigns, or graphic design work. Show us websites you shipped. — 2–3 case studies that walk us through your process: how you structured the site, what the wireframes looked like, how the final design connects back to the brief. The thinking matters as much as the output. — A short introduction: who you are, what kinds of projects you've worked on, and your hourly rate. *Applications without a process-driven case study will not be reviewed.*

systems • Interpret survey information accurately CAD Drafting • Prepare high-quality contour and detail plans • Draft as-built plans and related survey outputs • Produce clear and accurate deliverables in AutoCAD-based software • Maintain drafting standards and consistency Point Cloud Feature Extraction • Extract 2D and 3D features from LiDAR and scan data • Identify and interpret site features from point clouds and imagery • Work with supporting 360 imagery and scan walkthroughs Quality Assurance • Carry out internal QA checks on survey plans and extracted data • Review outputs for completeness, accuracy, and drafting quality • Assist in maintaining high production standards Additional Support • Assist with survey pre-calculations when required • Support ongoing workflow improvements and process optimisation • Collaborate with Australian surveyors and production staff Minimum Requirements: Essential • Bachelor’s Degree in Geodetic Engineering • Minimum 3 years’ experience in surveying • Minimum 50% of prior experience must be office-based • Strong experience using AutoCAD or similar CAD software • Experience reducing and drafting topographic / contour surveys • Strong understanding of survey drafting standards • Strong English communication skills • Reliable internet connection and professional home office setup • Available full-time (40 hours per week) • Able to work independently and follow structured workflows Technical Requirements You must either: • already have a computer setup capable of running AutoCAD and point cloud software efficiently OR • be willing to upgrade your computer setup to meet the technical requirements of the role Applicants must also provide computer/device specifications and equipment setup details, including CPU, RAM, GPU, storage, monitor setup, internet speed, headset/webcam, and home office setup. Highly Preferred • Field survey experience • Experience working on topographic / contour and detail surveys • Experience with point cloud workflows and LiDAR data • Experience with Australian surveying standards • Experience with survey QA processes • Experience with Civil 3D, Magnet, or point cloud software What We’re Looking For We are looking for someone who: • is an A-player who takes ownership, communicates proactively, and delivers high-quality work • is serious about long-term growth within a high-performing remote team • takes pride in producing accurate work • is detail-oriented and solutions-focused • enjoys technical workflows and digital surveying • communicates clearly and professionally • can work efficiently without sacrificing quality • wants long-term growth within a modern surveying business This is not an entry-level role. title: HR Manager
description: Job Title: Human Resources (HR) Manager Job Summary: We are seeking an experienced and dynamic Human Resources (HR) Manager to lead and direct our HR department's day-to-day operations. description: I’m looking for someone warm, socially intelligent, discreet, and thoughtful to help manage and grow a sensitive personal online presence across multiple platforms. This is not a typical social media VA role, and it is definitely not a spammy growth-hacking role. The goal is to build a presence that feels human, trustworthy, respectful, warm, and carefully positioned. This role would suit someone who naturally understands tone, people, community dynamics, and how small details can affect trust. You would help with multi-platform strategy, profile presentation, messaging, community research, and organizing leads/messages. A big part of the role is helping the profile show up consistently while still feeling authentic, calm, discreet, and not pushy. Main tasks may include: Researching Facebook groups, niche platforms, Instagram, and other possible channels Understanding community culture and group dynamics before posting Helping with profile positioning, image presentation, and overall trust signals Drafting posts, captions, and messages for review Organizing leads, messages, platforms, and follow-ups Suggesting ways to increase visibility without sounding spammy, desperate, defensive, or overly salesy Helping avoid unnecessary drama, especially in communities with politics, hostile comments, or sensitive dynamics Knowing when something should be engaged with, ignored, softened, clarified, or escalated You would not be expected to handle legal, medical, or highly sensitive conversations. You also would not reply to sensitive messages without approval. I care more about careful judgment than speed. The ideal person is someone who is: Warm, emotionally intelligent, and good with people Discreet and comfortable with sensitive/private topics Strong in written English Calm under group politics or hostile comments Proactive, but not reckless Careful with tone and wording Able to research online communities before engaging Good at making profiles feel trustworthy and human Organized enough to track leads, messages, platforms, and follow-ups Thoughtful about how things may be perceived by different people Experience with community management, client success, social media, online profiles, PR, Canva/graphics, or sensitive client-facing work is a plus. The best fit is someone who can act almost like a thoughtful right hand: helping create controlled, consistent visibility while protecting the tone, reputation, and trust of the profile. I’ll start with a small paid test task first. If it feels like a good fit on both sides, this can become ongoing part-time work. Please reply with: Your relevant experience Whether you are comfortable with sensitive/private profile topics How you would research a Facebook group before posting Your hourly rate and availability Your MBTI type

title: Hatchery Operations Manager
description: Mudcrab Hatchery Operations Manager Location: Himamaylan, Negros Occidental Reports To: Farm Owner Employment Type: Full-Time, Operational (requires on-call availability) About the Role: We are seeking a master of metamorphosis. This is not a routine farm management position; it is a highly specialized, science-driven role responsible for the most delicate phase of the mudcrab lifecycle. The Hatchery Operations Manager will orchestrate the entire hatchery process, from broodstock maturation to the delivery of healthy, robust crablets (megalopa/crabeon stage). You will blend deep knowledge of decapod biology with industrial facility management to solve a singular, critical challenge: reliably producing life at scale. Key Responsibilities: 1. Production Mastery & Larval Rearing Broodstock & Spawning: Manage the entire reproductive cycle, including broodstock selection, health assessment, conditioning, and spawning induction (including unilateral eyestalk ablation where applicable) of Scylla serrata and related species. Larval Lifecycle Management: Oversee the critical and fragile transition through all zoea stages (Z1-Z5) to megalopa and finally to crabelet. This includes managing metamorphosis, identifying staging in real-time, and adjusting protocols instantly. Live Feed Command: Direct the high-density, axenic (zero-contamination) production of the entire live feed chain—intensive microalgae (Nannochloropsis, Chaetoceros, Tetraselmis), rotifers (Brachionus), and Artemia—with a focus on targeted enrichment profiles (e.g., HUFA, Vitamin C) for each larval stage. 2. Industrial Systems & Water Quality Management Life Support Systems: Assume ownership of all Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and flow-through infrastructure. This includes hands-on troubleshooting and preventative maintenance of pumps, biofilters, protein skimmers, UV sterilizers, heaters/chillers, and emergency backup systems. Parameter Precision: Maintain a non-negotiable, 24/7 stable environment by monitoring and reacting to critical parameters: temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, pH, ammonia, nitrite, and alkalinity. Calibrate automated probes against manual titration methods regularly. 3. Biosecurity & Veterinary Health Disease Prevention: Act as the first line of defense. Implement and enforce a fortress-style biosecurity plan to prevent catastrophic events from pathogens like luminous vibriosis, Lagenidium fungus, and ciliates. Health Diagnostics: Perform daily microscopic health checks on larvae, identify early signs of stress, bacterial blooms, or necrosis, and execute rapid, decisive treatment protocols. Sanitation Protocols: Enforce rigorous dry-out, disinfection, and sterilization cycles for all tanks, equipment, and facilities between production runs. 4. Data, Science, and Continuous Improvement Forensic Record-Keeping: Maintain a meticulous, "black box" of data for every production run: survival rates by stage, daily feeding regimes, water chemistry logs, and growth metrics. This data is used to diagnose failures and replicate success. R&D for Cannibalism Mitigation: Lead ongoing applied research trials to crack the code on the megalopa-to-crablet bottleneck. This includes innovating with shelter designs (substrates, mesh structures), optimizing stocking densities, and manipulating environmental cues to reduce aggressive behavior and maximize survival. 5. Leadership & Emergency Response Team Leadership: Train and lead a small, dedicated team of technicians. Instill a culture of precision, cleanliness, and acute observation. Crisis Management: This is a 24/7 life-support operation. The manager must be mentally prepared to wake up, diagnose a failing pump, a drop in dissolved oxygen, or a disease outbreak, and make life-or-death decisions for millions of animals under extreme pressure. Candidate Profile: Are You One of the Few? Essential Technical Mastery Decapod Science: Deep, applied understanding of crustacean endocrinology, molting physiology, and nutritional pathology. Aquatic Engineering: You can rebuild a pump, wire a float switch, sweat PVC pipe, and diagnose a short-circuited blower. You are as comfortable with a wrench as with a microscope. Microscopic Eye: You can quickly identify a healthy Z3 larva from a bacterially infected one, and spot the difference between a rotifer and a ciliate bloom under a scope. Required Background Education: BSc or MSc in Aquaculture, Marine Biology, or related field. A proven track record can substitute for a degree. Experience: Minimum 5+ years in a marine hatchery, with at least 2 years in a supervisory role. Specialized Track Record: Must have direct, verifiable, hands-on experience closing the lifecycle of a decapod crustacean (mudcrab, swimming crab, shrimp/prawn). Experience with Scylla is the gold standard. Personal Attributes The "Biological Clock": You have an intuitive sense for the rhythm of a hatchery; you "feel" when something is wrong before the alarms go off. Resilient Problem-Solver: You remain calm and logical when a production run crashes, immediately shifting to root-cause analysis and solution mode. Guardian of Biosecurity: You have a slightly obsessive mindset about cleanliness and contamination control.

title: Aesthetic Content Creation / Instagram
description: Job Title: Aesthetic Social Media Content Creator (Western, Americana & Faith-Based) About the Role We are looking for a highly creative and visually-driven Social Media Content Creator to join our team. If you have an eye for cinematic, moody, and vintage aesthetics, and you know how to pair striking imagery with powerful typography, this role is for you. Our brand embodies a rugged, authentic lifestyle—focusing on Western culture, Americana, the great outdoors, and faith-based values. We are looking for someone who can translate this ethos into highly shareable, aesthetic social media posts that resonate deeply with our audience. What You’ll Do As our Social Media Content Creator, your primary responsibility will be visual storytelling. You will source, curate, or create high-quality, cinematic imagery that fits our brand’s rugged, outdoor, and Western aesthetic. A significant part of your daily workflow will involve photo editing and color grading. You must be able to apply consistent editing styles to photos to achieve a moody, vintage film look. This includes adding film grain, adjusting exposure for a darker and moody feel, and mastering desaturated, high-contrast color grading. We are not opposed to the use of AI, but it must be tasteful and unrecognizable. Beyond imagery, you will handle typography and layout. You will design graphic posts by overlaying bold, retro, and serif typography onto the imagery. You will be responsible for placing punchy, meaningful quotes about life, faith, and country living in a way that is visually striking and readable. Your goal is to maintain a highly curated and cohesive social media presence that aligns with our core identity, while also staying up-to-date with social media trends, aesthetic formats, and audio that align with our niche. What We’re Looking For We are seeking an individual with a strong aesthetic mastery. You should have a portfolio or personal feed showcasing moody, cinematic, film-grain, or vintage-style photo editing. Alongside your editing skills, you must possess an excellent eye for design and typography, understanding exactly which serif fonts give off that classic, nostalgic Americana feel. Technical proficiency in photo editing and design software, such as Adobe Lightroom, Photoshop, Illustrator, or advanced mobile editing applications, is required. Most importantly, you need a genuine cultural alignment with our brand. We want someone who understands and appreciates the Western lifestyle, vintage Americana, and faith-based messaging, allowing you to speak to this audience authentically. A strong copywriting sensibility to craft or select short, impactful quotes that perfectly match the mood of the imagery is essential.

title: Meta ads editor
description: VIDEO EDITOR (META ADS) Remote • Contract to Monthly Retainer BEFORE YOU APPLY It is important to fully understand who we are, where we stand, and the standard we hold before you move forward. This is not for everyone. We hire editors who hold a high standard, work fast, and want to build something real with a team that is scaling. We move fast and we expect you to keep up. The editors who thrive here want volume, real money, and work they are proud of. Before we tell you what the role looks like, here is who we are. WHO WE ARE Launch OS is the marketing engine behind high-ticket coaches, consultants, and other service based companies doing $150k to $800k+ per month. We are a done-for-you marketing partner. We take full ownership of our clients' growth: paid ads, full-funnel builds, CRM and automation, email and SMS, webinars, challenges, and the creative that fuels all of it. Our entire system runs on one framework, the Modern Marketing Method: Offer, Leads, Sales, Fulfillment. Video ads sit at the front of that machine. They are the first thing a prospect sees, and they decide whether the rest of the system ever gets a chance to work. That is where you come in. The ads you edit go straight in front of paying clients' audiences and directly create their revenue. In a nutshell, we build predictable ad engines for our clients, and high-quality edits are an important part of making sure those ads convert. OUR MISSION Bring the good guys back. The businesses built on ethics and grit, the ones who do things right but still get overlooked while louder, shadier operators cut corners. Those are the people we fight for, because business can be both ethical and wildly profitable. OUR CORE VALUES Simplicity is Sophistication The smartest solution is usually the simplest one. Anyone can make things complicated. It takes real skill to make them simple. One of Zero Say what others can't and do what others won't. Authenticity Wins People smell bullshit from a mile away. Just be real. Resourcefulness Not Resources "I don't know" is never an answer. Use the tools at your disposal. Get it done. Obsess Over Value + Extreme Ownership Make people's lives better. Own every result, good or bad. Always ask: "How does this help them?" No Boring S*** Life's too short for boring ideas. If it doesn't spark something in you, why should anyone else care? WHO THIS IS FOR • An editor who lives and breathes short-form vertical video ads built for Meta (Facebook and Instagram) • Someone who can edit 20 ads in 48 to 72 hours while keeping the quality high • Someone who keeps edits engaging and simple. Over-editing kills ads • Someone who uses AI to speed up the work and knows the difference between a clean edit and AI slop WHAT WE EXPECT • Edit scroll-stopping Meta video ads that hold attention from the first frame • Know music and sound design. The right track, clean audio, and background levels that sit properly under a voiceover • Know b-roll and motion graphics. When to use them, how long to hold them on screen, and when to leave them out. Motion should serve the message • Build engaging cuts and pacing that feel intentional. Tight, clean, and easy to follow • Zero spelling errors. Captions and on-screen text get checked every single time OUR STANDARD ON AI • AI is allowed where it genuinely helps • No Remotion plus Claude editing. Edits are done manually • Anything that looks like AI slop does not ship THE BASICS • Timeliness. You hit deadlines without being chased • Self-sufficient with strong time management • Detail-oriented. You catch the small things before we do • Fast, clear communication • You take full ownership. You own your misses and improve fast NON-NEGOTIABLES • Hit every deadline, every time • Do what you say you are going to do • No spelling or text errors in delivered work • Manual editing, no AI slop • Show up prepared and communicate fast • Do not do the minimum HOW THIS WORKS We do not hire off a resume. We hire off the work. Step 1: The Paid Trial Edit We send you one unedited ad. You edit it and return it within a 24-hour turnaround. This is paid (see below). We are watching for speed, quality judgment, and attention to detail. Step 2: The Paid Engagement If the trial edit is done properly, we move straight into a paid engagement, starting with a batch of 20 to 30 video ads to edit. From there it becomes an ongoing monthly relationship based on volume and performance. WHAT IS INCLUDED • The written script for the video ad • The raw footage of the ad • Examples of quality ads our current team has done WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR • Timeliness • A real understanding of what quality looks like • Highly engaging edits that stay simple, clean, and intentional • No spelling errors • Someone detail-oriented who knows how to create cuts and edits that hold attention PAY • $50 for the single trial edit • After the trial, $1,500 to $3,500 per month depending on total volume The better and faster you are, the more volume comes your way, and the more you make. The work is steady, the team is scaling, and you can do all of it from anywhere. HOW TO APPLY We will be hiring off the work, not the resume. When you apply, include the following: • A link to your portfolio or reel, leading with the short-form vertical video ads you have edited for Meta (Facebook and Instagram) • 2 to 3 direct links to individual ads you edited, with one line on each explaining exactly what you did • The software and tools you edit in • Your honest turnaround on a single ad, and whether you can hold 20 ads in a 48 to 72 hour window without the quality slipping • One line on how you use AI in your workflow To confirm you read this whole post, start your message with the word "Greenlight" and tell us one thing in your editing process that you refuse to compromise on, no matter the deadline. title: Product Manager
description: What you'll own Each of our clients is an AI consumer company trying to turn a launch into pipeline. Your job is to own one of those launches end-to-end - we call this a play. A play is a 6-8 week campaign: you pick the creators, write the brief, ship the content, watch the metrics, kill what's not working, double down on what is. Most plays drive 50K-500K installs or signups for the AI product. You are the single throat to choke for one product's launch. You own the outcome. What you'll actually do Define the launch hypothesis. What's the user behavior change this product is betting on? Who's the early adopter? What's the hook that gets them in the door? Source creators. You find your own creators - 10-30 per week in the product's niche across TikTok, IG, and YouTube Shorts. We give you the sourcing tools, the existing creator database (50K+), and the criteria. There is no separate sourcer; the play is yours end-to-end. Brief and ship. Write the creative brief, send the assignments, answer creator questions in our shared Slack channels. Get content out the door fast. Measure and iterate. Track posts, views, conversions. Run experiments on hook, format, and CTA. Weekly decisions on what to kill and what to scale. Report. Weekly written update on the play: what shipped, what we learned, what's next. Direct dialogue with the client founder. Who this is for This page exists because we believe great operators get priced out of the global tech market for reasons that have nothing to do with their ability. We want to find them and pay them fairly for the value they create, while building the most diverse and capable PM team in creator marketing. Self-taught is welcome. We do not care about which university you went to or any school credential. Show us what you've shipped and what you watch and how you think. Ships things. You have launched something. A TikTok account, a Shopify store, a Discord community, a Substack, a side product. Anything where you had to make 100 small decisions and learn from outcomes. Lives on short-form video. You can name 5 creator accounts you follow in different niches and explain exactly why each one works. Bonus if some are South East Asian creators - we want that local context. AI-native. You don't just use ChatGPT. You build small things with Claude, Cursor, v0, Lovable, ElevenLabs, Runway. Whatever the job needs. Comfortable with async + overlap hours. Most work is on your own schedule, but you can do 2-4 hours of US or EU overlap a few times a week for client calls. What you have shipped matters more than any school you went to. What you'll get Paid in USD. $400-$600/month base depending on hours and experience, plus performance bonus tied to your play's outcomes. The bonus can be larger than the base for top performers, paid in USD via Wise or Payoneer. Real ownership. You own one product's launch, then 2-3 as you ramp. Your name on the work, directly visible to the founders of the AI products we're launching. The 8x playbook. Every internal SOP, every creator network, every tool. We hand you what took 18 months to build. Direct path to extend. 3-month role to start. Top performers extend or convert to permanent roles at increased comp. Mentorship from the team. Weekly 1:1 with the head of plays. Direct line to the CEO when you need it. The same operating context the EU team gets. $3M+ Run rate 100k+ Creators in network 30+ Countries About 8x Social 8x Social is the infrastructure layer for performance-driven creator marketing. We work with the fastest-growing AI consumer companies to turn their launches into pipeline, connecting them with 100k+ creators across 30+ countries. Founded by Jaka Bavdek (CEO, London Business School) and Theo Bui (CTO, Imperial College), we're backed by Entrepreneur First and based in San Francisco. We're the fastest-growing company in EF history. We are explicitly building a globally distributed PM team because we believe talent is everywhere even when opportunity isn't. If you want to operate on real AI launches with full ownership, this is the most direct way in.

description: ABOUT THE ROLE We're a growing home health agency in Ohio looking for an exceptional HR Director to own our people function end-to-end — recruiting, onboarding, compliance, retention, employee relations, and the systems that hold it all together. Caregiver turnover is the single biggest challenge in our industry. If you've moved that number at a previous home health, home care, hospice, or skilled nursing employer, you're who we want to talk to. This is a remote, full-time, senior seat. You'll be the most senior HR voice in the company, working directly with the CEO and operations leadership. The work is high-trust, high-judgment, and high-impact. We're hiring one person — we want it to be the right person. This industry has rules that take years to learn. - SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR certification (or active, documented progress toward one) - Demonstrated track record of reducing caregiver or clinical-staff turnover at a previous employer — be ready to talk specific numbers - Working knowledge of CMS Conditions of Participation for home health, OASIS workflows, and Medicare/Medicaid compliance touchpoints that intersect with HR - Hands-on experience with HRIS / ATS / payroll platforms (Paychex, ADP, Paylocity, BambooHR, Workable, Greenhouse, or similar) - Bulletproof written English — you'll author policies, handbooks, investigation memos, and disciplinary documentation that have to stand up to legal scrutiny - Calm, confidential, and decisive in employee relations situations - Comfortable being the senior HR voice in the company and pushing back on the CEO when the law or the policy requires it - Comfortable signing an NDA and completing HIPAA training before day one WORK ENVIRONMENT (NON-NEGOTIABLE): - Reliable high-speed internet (minimum 25 Mbps down / 10 Mbps up) - Quiet, professional workspace - USB headset and a working webcam - A primary device on supported OS (Windows 11 or macOS) SCHEDULE AND COMPENSATION: - Full-time, 40 hours/week - Eastern Time business hours, primary overlap 9 AM – 5 PM ET - $8–10 USD/hour, depending on experience and certifications - 10 paid days off per year - Annual performance review with a defined raise framework DO NOT APPLY IF: - You don't have direct home health, home care, hospice, post-acute, or skilled nursing HR experience - You're currently juggling another full-time role - You're more comfortable executing tactics than owning strategy — this is a director seat, not a coordinator role - You're not comfortable with confidential information, NDAs, or HIPAA-style training HOW TO APPLY: Send the following: 1. Your résumé. 2. A brief written description (3–6 sentences) telling us why you'd be a great fit for this specific role. 3. A short video (1–2 minutes) telling us why you're the best person for this and what sets you apart from the others. 4. A short story (5–8 sentences) about a specific turnover or retention problem you solved at a previous employer — what the metric was before, what you changed, what the metric was after, and how long it took. title: Customer Success Lead
description: ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Customer Success Lead to own post-sale customer outcomes for sales-assisted and high-value merchants. You will help customers launch successfully, prove the system is working in production, resolve risks before they become major escalations, prepare for renewals, and expand into new states, categories, platforms, or workflows. You’ll coordinate with Operations, Product, Engineering, and Growth. This is a player/coach role, so team guidance and process improvement may be part of the role, but direct reports are not guaranteed. WHAT THIS ROLE IS AND IS NOT This is not a basic CSM role focused mainly on check-ins and relationship maintenance. This is not a reactive support queue role. This role sits in the middle of customer outcomes, onboarding, compliance confidence, risk management, renewal readiness, expansion readiness, and internal coordination. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to be comfortable using evidence, customer context, and structured follow-through to move complex accounts forward. ABOUT TOKEN OF TRUST Token of Trust helps regulated eCommerce businesses keep selling with confidence. We help merchants launch compliant checkout, verify customers when required, reduce compliance risk, and manage the reporting and evidence they need to operate in regulated markets. Customers have rated Token of Trust 4.9 stars on G2, and G2 recognized us among the 2026 Top 50 Data Privacy Products. We have also been recognized for Best Support, Easiest To Do Business With, High Performer, and Users Most Likely To Recommend. Customer Success is a core part of why customers trust us. We are looking for someone who wants to help customers succeed while also improving the systems, playbooks, and processes behind that success. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Own the customer experience after sale: onboarding, launch, first proof of value, ongoing operations, renewal readiness, and expansion readiness - Help customers launch compliant checkout with clear milestones, owners, risks, and next steps - Help customers reach their first real proof of value in production, such as a successfully cleared customer, order, report, or compliance workflow - Monitor customer risks such as verification issues, reporting problems, misconfiguration risk, unresolved blockers, or customer confusion - Lead escalations by gathering evidence, isolating the problem, coordinating the right internal owners, and keeping customers updated - Help customers understand and trust compliance calculations, reporting outputs, verification states, and operational workflows - Prepare high-value accounts for renewal 60 to 90 days in advance by surfacing risks and driving issue-resolution plans - Support customer expansion into new states, categories, platforms, or workflows - Capture customer feedback clearly, ideally in the customer’s own words, and turn it into product feedback, internal tickets, or playbook improvements - Improve onboarding playbooks, SOPs, help docs, and internal processes WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE You are successful when customers: - Launch without unnecessary delays or rework - Reach their first clear proof that Token of Trust is working for them - Know whether their workflow is configured correctly because there is evidence, not just reassurance - Avoid preventable surprises or unresolved escalations - Enter renewals with known issues, owners, timelines, and a clear value story - Feel that Token of Trust is organized, proactive, and clear We care about support quality and customer sentiment, but this role is not measured mainly by ticket count, meeting count, logins, or generic activity metrics. GROWTH OPPORTUNITY For the right person, this is a real growth path, not just a customer-facing seat. As you prove judgement, ownership, and customer outcome discipline, you can earn more trust, broader responsibility, and increased compensation over time. Possible growth paths include: - Owning high-value customer onboarding and renewal readiness programs - Building better proof-of-value playbooks for new customers - Improving customer risk visibility and escalation prevention - Creating customer health, renewal, and expansion workflows - Guiding other tea ---------- mbers through shared-account or playbook-driven Success work - Becoming a deeper expert in regulated eCommerce customer outcomes MUST-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS - 4+ years in B2B SaaS Customer Success, Implementation, Solutions, Technical Account Management, or complex customer support - Experience owning post-sale outcomes such as onboarding, go-live, risk management, renewal readiness, or expansion support - Excellent written English - Strong organization and follow-through - Ability to manage multiple customer issues without losing details - Good judgement in ambiguous, technical, regulated, or high-stakes situations - Comfortable coordinating across Operations, Product, Engineering, and Growth without formal authority - Able to diagnose issues clearly: what changed, what is the impact, what evidence exists, and what should happen next NICE TO HAVE - Experience in regulated eCommerce, identity verification, KYC, fraud, payments risk, tax, compliance reporting, or trust and safety - Experience with Shopify, WooCommerce/WordPress, or headless eCommerce - Basic understanding of webhooks, APIs, event logs, or technical troubleshooting - Experience creating SOPs, playbooks, customer help docs, or internal process improvements - Experience with shared-account or team-based customer success models YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU - Like complex products where correctness and evidence matter - Can lead escalations calmly without overpromising - Prefer customer outcomes over activity metrics - Enjoy improving systems, not just answering questions - Communicate clearly with both customers and internal teams THIS MAY NOT BE A FIT IF YOU - Want a simple reactive support role - Prefer highly defined work with little ambiguity - Dislike cross-functional coordination - Rely mostly on meetings, logins, or ticket counts to measure customer success - Struggle to keep many open customer issues organized TOOLS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT We use tools such as Amplitude, internal database reporting, FreeScout, Stripe, Pipedrive, G2, Shopify/WordPress ecosystems, shared docs, issue trackers, and internal playbooks. You do not need experience with every tool, but you must be comfortable learning new systems quickly. The work is remote, technical, compliance-heavy, and documentation-heavy. You’ll work with Operations, Product, Engineering, and Growth. SCHEDULE - Minimum 20 hours per week required - Opportunity to expand to full-time, 40 hours per week, based on business needs, role fit, and performance - Remote - Meaningful overlap with U.S. business hours required - Please include your timezone and preferred working hours when applying COMPENSATION This role starts at approximately $300 per month for a minimum schedule of 20 hours per week. There is an opportunity to increase both hours and earnings over time. The role may expand to full-time, and strong performers may also qualify for monthly performance incentives. Target total monthly earnings can increase to approximately $450 to $750 per month depending on hours, performance, role scope, and business needs. Please include your expected monthly compensation in your application. HOW TO APPLY Use this subject line: Customer Success Lead: I help customers prove value Please send: 1) Resume or LinkedIn profile 2) Compensation and availability - Expected monthly compensation - Timezone - Preferred working hours - Amount of overlap you can provide with U.S. business hours 3) Customer ownership story In 5 to 8 sentences, describe one complex customer workflow, onboarding, renewal-risk, or escalation situation you owned end-to-end. Tell us what happened, what you did, how you knew whether the customer was getting value, and what changed as a result. 4) Process improvement example Briefly describe one playbook, SOP, customer health process, renewal process, or internal handoff you improved. 5) Short written exercise A customer says: “We turned this on and now good customers are getting stuck. We are worried this will hurt conversion.” Please answer: - What would you say in your first customer-facing reply? - What information would you gather internally? - Who would you involve internally and why? - How would you keep the customer updated over the next 48 to 72 hours? 6) AI usage note Tell us how you used AI, if at all, to complete this application: - Which sections did AI help with? - Where did you rely on your own judgment? - How did you verify the final answer reflected your actual experience and thinking? Applications that do not follow these instructions may not be reviewed. HIRING PROCESS After initial application review, selected candidates may be asked to confirm role requirements, compensation fit, long-term interest, no agency or subcontracting relationship, time-tracking expectations, background-check willingness, and integrity expectations. Finalists may be asked to complete a short intro video and a paid trial project before final interviews.

title: Automation & Systems Specialist - Remote (Part-Time / Project-Based)
description: Flexible hours | Remote | Microsoft 365, Power Platform & Workflow Automation If you enjoy turning messy, manual workflows into clean automated systems, and you like solving real operational problems, this could be a good fit. Platinum Healthcare has been supporting Perth communities since 2006. We work across NDIS, aged care, Support at Home, recruitment, and business support. Our coordinators handle a high volume of email : clinical notes from external providers, task requests, and automatic alerts from our scheduling and client management system. We want to automate the triage, summarising, record-keeping, and filing of that email so coordinators spend less time on noise and more time on clients. This is a part-time or project-based role. We are not sure we have enough work to keep someone busy full-time, so we want someone who can scope, build, document, and hand over a working system, then stay available for the next phase. You will design and build the automations yourself, not just advise. What This Role Is Really Like This is a build role, not a pure advisory one. You will look at how email and alerts currently flow to our coordinators, design a better process, and build it in our Microsoft 365 environment. You will work under our governance: we control the credentials, the environment access, and any write-back to live client records. You build inside that, document what you build, and train us to run it. The work blends: • workflow design and process mapping • Power Automate flow building • AI-based classification and summarisation • API and custom connector integration • documentation and handover The Work A current example of what we want built: • Coordinators receive every email and system alert in one inbox. We want each new message classified: does the coordinator need to do anything, is there a deterioration or input request, what is the urgency. • We want a short, clear summary produced for the coordinator on items that need action. • Where an email is an external clinical update, we want a note or document created in the matching client record in our system (Sandwai) via its API. • Once an email is processed, we want it moved to an archive folder automatically. • We want a manual-review path for anything the automation cannot match or classify with confidence, so nothing is written to the wrong client. You would design this as a staged build: a quick win first (triage and summary), then system integration, then governance and audit controls. We expect you to recommend the right sequence. What We're Looking For • Strong, demonstrated experience building automations in Microsoft Power Automate • Experience with Microsoft 365 and Outlook / shared mailbox automation • Experience calling REST APIs and building or configuring custom connectors • Experience using AI / prompt-based steps for text classification and summarisation (AI Builder, Copilot Studio, or similar) • Able to design a sensible process, not just wire up tools • Clear documentation and handover skills, so we can run and maintain what you build • Comfortable working within client governance and least-privilege access, especially around health data • Able to work independently, scope your own work, and manage priorities remotely • Copilot Studio, Dataverse, or SharePoint experience is an advantage • Healthcare, NDIS, aged care, or compliance exposure is advantageous but not essential Hours & Structure • Part-time or project-based, remote • Hours flexible and scoped to the work in front of us • Initial engagement is to scope and build the email automation described above • Ongoing or repeat work likely for the right person as we automate more workflows What We Offer • Remote work flexibility • Clearly defined projects with real operational impact • Supportive and approachable leadership • Direct communication and a team that values your contribution • A pipeline of further automation work as systems mature How to Apply Please apply with: • Your CV/resume • A short cover letter about your background In your cover letter, please answer the following: • Describe an automation you built end to end in Power Automate. What problem did it solve, and how did you handle errors or exceptions? • Have you integrated a third-party system via API or custom connector? Tell us what and how. • This role involves health-related client data. How do you approach handling sensitive data and working within someone else's access controls? • This is part-time or project-based rather than ongoing full-time. What interests you about that kind of arrangement?

title: UAT Tester (Contract) - No Graveyard Shift
description: # UAT Tester (Contract), Zelix Labs **Engagement:** Contract / freelance **Level:** Mid-level **Location:** Remote (Singapore hours, SGT, with overlap expected) **Reports to:** Product lead / Project owner ## About Zelix Labs Zelix Labs builds conversational AI and automation for businesses: WhatsApp flows, AI agents, client portals, booking and intake systems, and the web layers around them. These go live in front of real clients and their customers, so the last check before launch matters as much as the build. ## The role We are hiring a mid-level UAT tester on contract to be that last check. You will run user acceptance testing across our web and automation projects: confirming features do what the brief said, catching the breaks before clients do, and writing them up so a developer can fix them without a back-and-forth. You think like the end user, not like the person who built it. ## What you will do - Read the brief or acceptance criteria, then turn them into clear, repeatable test cases. - Run UAT across web apps, forms, dashboards, WhatsApp flows, and automation sequences. - Test the full journey, not just the happy path: edge cases, bad input, broken links, mobile and desktop, different browsers. - Verify integrations end to end (form to CRM, webhook to automation, payment confirmation, message delivery). - Log defects clearly: steps to reproduce, expected vs actual, screenshots or recordings, severity. - Re-test fixes and confirm nothing else broke (regression). - Sign off on what is ready to ship, and be straight about what is not. - Keep a tidy test record so we have evidence of what was checked. ## What we are looking for - Two or more years in QA or UAT testing, ideally on web or SaaS products. - Strong eye for detail. You notice the thing everyone else scrolled past. - Able to write test cases and bug reports that a developer can act on without a call. - Comfortable testing across browsers, devices, and screen sizes. - Understands the difference between a bug, a missing requirement, and a design choice, and reports each correctly. - Methodical and organised. You finish the checklist. - Clear written English. You will work async, so your write-ups have to stand on their own. ## Nice to have - Experience testing automation or chatbot flows (WhatsApp, ---------- , GoHighLevel, n8n, ---------- ). - Familiarity with a defect tracker (Asana, Jira, Notion, or similar). - Basic API testing (Postman or similar) to check integrations directly. - Some exposure to test automation tools, though this role is primarily manual UAT. ## How we work together You will get the build, the acceptance criteria, and access to a defect tracker. We treat a well-written bug report as a gift, not a complaint. We would rather you flag ten things and have two turn out fine than miss the one that reaches the client. Honest sign-off is the whole job; never wave something through to keep the peace. ## To apply Send a short note, your testing experience, and a sample bug report or test plan you have written (redacted is fine). Availability and rate expectations welcome up front.

title: Founder's Associate, Operations & Systems (Startup Gaming Niche)
job_title: Founder's Associate, Operations & Systems (Startup Gaming Niche)
description: **About us** We're a small, fast-moving team in the video game industry. We're growing quickly, we treat our people well, and we play the long game: clear expectations, steady work, genuine respect, and real growth for those who earn it. This is a seat to build a career in, not a churn-and-burn gig. We're looking for someone exceptional to grow with us. **What this role is** You'll be the right hand to seasoned founders who move fast and never run out of ideas, which is exactly why this role exists. Your job is to bring order to that: take things off the plate, build the systems that keep the business running, and turn loose goals into finished work. Sometimes you'll have a clear process to follow. Just as often, you won't, and that's where the right person shines. When there's no playbook, you research it, figure out the smartest way to do it, talk it through with the founders, build the process, and then act on it. A real example of what we mean: "We need to bring on a video editor. Figure out where to find good ones, what it should cost, screen the candidates, bring me your top picks, and once we approve, get them onboarded and working." That's the level of ownership we're after. We want to hand you a goal and trust it's handled, not assign you a checklist. If you bring problems wrapped in solutions instead of just questions, you'll thrive here. If you need step-by-step instructions for everything, this isn't the fit. We'll have a short check-in call once a day during the initial period to stay aligned, get you up to speed on how we work, unblock you quickly, and move quickly together. **What you'll do** It varies week to week, but expect a mix of: - Building SOPs and systems: Turning the things we do into clean, written, repeatable processes so the business runs more smoothly over time. This is a core part of the job, not an afterthought. - Acting on those systems: Running and following up on recurring work so nothing slips, and keeping our internal systems tidy and up to date. - Project management: Owning one-off projects end-to-end: scoping them, driving them, and reporting back clearly. - Hiring support: Sourcing, screening, and helping onboard contractors and tea ---------- mbers as we grow. - Content posting: Publishing and organizing content across our channels on a consistent schedule. - Coordination: Working with vendors, contractors, and our team to keep things moving. - Research: Figuring out the best way to do something we've never done, then bringing back a clear recommendation. The specific tools and tasks are learnable, and we'll teach you what's specific to us. What we can't teach is the resourcefulness and drive to own the outcome. **Who you are** - Resourceful: When you hit something you don't know, you figure it out. You research, you learn, and you come back with a plan, not just a question. - Proactive and ownership-driven: You anticipate what's needed, follow through without reminders, and treat the business as if it were your own. - Organized and systems-minded: You think in processes and checklists. You like building order out of chaos and enjoy finding smarter ways to do things. - Comfortable with ambiguity: A sharp, fast learner who can take a vague goal and find the path forward. - An excellent communicator: in written and spoken English, clear, professional, and easy to work with. You'll talk to the founders directly and represent us with vendors and contractors. - Hungry, with high standards and a strong work ethic: This matters to us more than your résumé. You take pride in your work, and you don't cut corners. - Honest, discreet, and trustworthy: You'll handle sensitive information. **Nice to have** These are bonuses, not requirements. Tell us if you have any of them: - 2+ years supporting founders, executives, or businesses - Fluent with AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. We love people who use them to move faster - Experience with Google Workspace, Notion, Trello, or similar - Experience writing SOPs or documenting processes - Hiring or recruiting experience - Content creation or light video editing **The details** - Hours: Full-time, with some daily overlap with British Summer Time. We'll work out the exact hours together. - Pay: 40,000 PHP - Payment: Weekly or biweekly via PayPal, Wise, Payoneer, or similar. - Location: Fully remote, work from home. - Type: Long-term. We want someone to build a future with us, and strong performers grow quickly from here. **How to apply** Please don't send copy-pasted applications. We read every complete one, and generic ones get ignored. One step: Record a short Loom or YouTube video** (a few minutes, on your own time) telling us: - A quick introduction about yourself and your relevant experience - Do you have any experience with video games? If so, which games do you play? - A time you were handed something with little or no instruction, and you figured it out and got it done - Why this role excites you and what makes you the person we're looking for We reply to every application that's a fit. We're excited to meet you.

title: E-Learning Module Production Specialist
description: About the Project We are producing 8 self-paced virtual learning modules (plus one short orientation module) for a professional development project in K-12 education. The full series is produced in both English and Spanish (18 modules total: 9 English + 9 Spanish). The English modules will be produced first. Scope of Work You will be responsible for four production phases per module: Phase 1: AI Voice Generation (ElevenLabs) • Generate narrated audio from finalized, slide-by-slide narration scripts using ElevenLabs text-to-speech • Each module contains 15-20 slides, each with its own narration block (total ~1,500-2,800 words per module) • Match voice settings (stability, clarity, style) to a reference sample we will provide for Module 1 in each language • Export individual audio files per slide (labeled by slide number) • QC each clip for mispronunciations, pacing issues, and unnatural breaks, especially on education-specific terminology (IEP, ESSA, IDEA, WIDA, and state-specific acronyms) • For Spanish modules: QC audio for artifacts, pacing, and unnatural breaks (translated scripts and linguistic review are handled separately) • Re-generate and splice as needed until each clip meets quality standards • A pronunciation guide is provided with every narration script Phase 2: iSpring Suite Assembly • Import the completed .pptx slide deck into iSpring Suite Max (desktop application, Windows required) • Sync generated audio to each slide with correct timing • Configure slide transitions and advance settings (audio-driven, not click-to-advance) • Preview and test full module playback end-to-end Phase 3: Accessibility QA • Verify reading order in PowerPoint (Selection Pane) matches logical content flow on every slide • Write or refine alt text for all images, graphics, and diagrams based on provided descriptions • Verify caption transcript files align with final audio (timing, content match) • Run color contrast checks on all text and background combinations (minimum 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text per WCAG 2.1 AA) • Confirm all non-text information conveyed by color also has a non-color indicator (labels, patterns, icons) • Test keyboard/tab navigation in the published module to ensure all content is reachable without a mouse • Log all findings in an accessibility checklist per module Phase 4: SCORM Packaging and QA • Publish each module as a SCORM 1.2 package (or SCORM 2004 if specified) • Configure completion tracking rules (e.g., viewed all slides) • Configure resume behavior (learner can exit and return where they left off) • Test the published SCORM package in SCORM Cloud or equivalent LMS test environment • Verify: audio plays correctly on all slides, completion triggers properly, package resumes on re-entry • Deliver the final .zip SCORM package and a brief QA checklist per module Deliverables Per Module 1. Audio files (one per slide, .mp3, labeled) 2. Published SCORM .zip package (tested and verified) 3. Accessibility checklist per module (reading order, alt text, contrast, keyboard nav) 4. Brief QA log noting any issues found and resolved during testing What We Provide • Finalized PowerPoint slide deck (.pptx) for each module • Finalized narration script with slide-by-slide text, word counts, and pronunciation guide • Storyboard with slide-by-slide specs • ElevenLabs voice profile and settings (configured after Module 1 approval) • iSpring Suite Max license (or you may use your own) • Access to a test LMS environment for SCORM verification Requirements Must have: • Hands-on experience with iSpring Suite (not just iSpring Free or iSpring Converter) • Experience publishing SCORM packages and testing in an LMS • Familiarity with ElevenLabs or equivalent AI voice tools • Windows computer (iSpring Suite is Windows-only) • Strong attention to detail, especially audio-to-slide sync • Comfortable working independently from written specs Nice to have: • Background in education, training, or instructional design • Experience with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility in e-learning (alt text, reading order, captions, contrast) • Familiarity with SCORM Cloud for testing • Experience producing modules for government or K-12 clients Timeline and Volume Detail Value Total modules 18 (9 English + 9 Spanish) Pricing and turnaround Fixed rate per module (3 business day turnaround) Test module Module 1 (English) is a paid test before full commitment English completion August 2026 Spanish completion September 2026 Modules will be delivered in batches as content is finalized, not all at once. Strong performers will be considered for ongoing work on future continuing professional development (CPD) course production. How to Apply Please include in your response: 1. Your experience with iSpring Suite (which version, how many modules produced) 2. Your experience with ElevenLabs or AI voice generation 3. A sample or description of a SCORM package you have produced 4. Your fixed rate per module and estimated turnaround time per module 5. Your availability through September 2026

We help shop owners streamline their workflow, reduce administrative stress, and increase profitability through a combination of smart systems and human support. Our core service revolves around Virtual Service Advisors (VSAs) who handle customer communication, booking triage, job approvals, and workflow optimisation. We also build internal tools, marketing assets, and client-facing platforms to support that mission, and that’s where you come in. If you have ever sat in a project watching developers make the design decisions, knowing you could have made the product genuinely better if someone had just handed you the keys, this role was written for you. We are upgrading our Elite Platform, a software platform used by Australian auto workshops, and we are looking for one designer to own how it looks and how it works, from the first wireframe to the final build-ready file. Right now, our developers are designing as they build. It works, but it means constant revisions and a look that drifts from screen to screen. We want someone to step in and bring it all together into one clear, consistent, genuinely usable product. The users are real mechanics and service advisors with grease on their hands and no patience for clutter, so the work is about clarity and flow, not decoration. This starts as a 3-month full-time project to design and ship Elite V2. When you prove this is your thing, it becomes a permanent role, with you owning the look and feel of everything we build from then on. This is you - You have designed real B2B SaaS or web apps, and Figma feels like home. - You look at a cluttered, complicated screen and you actually enjoy finding the simple version hiding inside it. - You design for the person using the product, not to impress other designers, and you can explain the thinking behind a choice instead of just saying it looks better. - You have opinions, and you hold them lightly. Feedback makes your work sharper, not defensive. - You think in systems. Sitemaps, navigation, and a clean component library are how your mind already works. - You are done with short gigs. You want somewhere to settle in, take ownership, and watch something get better because of you. If you read that and felt a quiet yes, keep going. What you will do day to day - Turn our team’s ideas into complete, ready-to-build designs. - Create wireframes and high-fidelity clickable prototypes in Figma. - Build and maintain a design system so every screen feels like part of the same product. - Design clear layouts for data-heavy screens like tables, dashboards, scheduling calendars, inventory, and financial reports. - Make designs work beautifully across desktop, tablet, and mobile. - Hand developers clean files, assets, and documentation they can build from accurately. - Run simple usability checks so problems get caught before a line of code is written. One real ---------- nt from the role The messy workflow A workshop needs to invoice one repair job that involved three different parts, two mechanics, and a follow-up booking. The developers hand you a cluttered screen with everything crammed in. How do you redesign it so a busy service advisor reads it in seconds and misses nothing? If your mind has already started solving that, picturing the layout, d ---------- what to cut, you are the person we are looking for. That instinct matters to us far more than a polished resume. Why you will like it here - You own the whole product, not a corner of it. The design is yours to shape. - 100% remote. Work from anywhere in the Philippines. - Australian day-shift hours, so your evenings and your family time stay yours. - Competitive pay in AUD, paid straight to your bank account. - Real growth. Strong performers move from project work into a permanent, long-term role. - A team that respects clear thinking and good design, and actually listens to its designer. What you will need - Solid experience designing B2B SaaS or web apps. A portfolio link is required. - Expert-level Figma, with wireframing, prototyping, design systems, and developer handoff. - Strong written and spoken English. - A reliable computer that runs Figma smoothly, a stable internet (tell us your real speed), and a quiet space for calls. How to apply Applications are only reviewed through the form below, not by email or through this post. Apply here: ---------- Select “UI/UX Designer” as the position. Two things we read first, so please do not skip them: 1. Share your portfolio link, and point us to one B2B SaaS or web app screen you are proud of. 2. Tell us about one complex interface you simplified. What was messy, and how did you solve it? Describe it for us. Do not just list it.
